definition_zh: 批准；通过；赞成；认可；认可某人适合
definition_en: to officially agree to or permit something, or to think that someone or something is good
core_image: 把一枚写着「可以」的印记盖到纸上
scene: 校长办公室里，一叠课程方案放在桌上。 The committee voted to approve the new course in the spring.
sceneCN: 这里 approve 是「批准；通过」（第 1 个义项：正式同意某事）；句意为「委员会投票通过了春季的新课程」。画面里有校长办公室、成叠的方案与投票用的纸片。

pos.zh: 动词：批准；通过；赞成；认可

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -al 构成，义为「批准；赞许；支持率」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「已获批准的；认可的」
由现在分词转作形容词，义为「赞许的」
由 approving 加 -ly 构成，义为「赞许地」
由 dis- 加本词构成，义为「不赞成」

senses.title: To give official permission
senses.definition: to officially agree to or permit a plan, request, or action
senses.definitionCN: 正式同意或允许某项计划、请求或行动
senses.example: The committee voted to approve the new course in the spring.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会投票通过了春季的新课程。
senses.why: Latin approbare was to give something the mark of good, and a committee does exactly that with a proposal.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 approbare 是给某物打上「好」的记号，委员会对提案所做的正是这件事。

senses.title: To think well of something
senses.definition: to consider someone or something good, right, or acceptable
senses.definitionCN: 认为某人某物是好的、正确的或可接受的
senses.example: Her parents do not approve of the late nights.
senses.exampleCN: 她的父母不赞成她熬夜。
senses.why: The stamp is given by opinion rather than by office.
senses.whyCN: 这枚印记由意见而不是职权盖下。

senses.title: To judge someone fit
senses.definition: to accept someone as suitable for a role, award, or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 接受某人适合某个角色、奖项或用途
senses.example: The board approved him for the scholarship.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会认可他获得这项奖学金。
senses.why: To approve a person is to judge him fit and mark him so.
senses.whyCN: 认可一个人，就是判断他合适，并给他打上这个记号。

senses.title: To permit official use
senses.definition: to give official permission for a product, medicine, or practice to be used
senses.definitionCN: 正式允许某种产品、药物或做法投入使用
senses.example: The drug was approved for children last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药去年获批用于儿童。
senses.why: Official bodies stamp products as good before the public may use them.
senses.whyCN: 官方机构先给产品盖上「好」的印记，公众才能使用。

intro.en: Approve is a Latin verb of testing and marking good, brought to English through French.
intro.cn: approve 是一个表示检验并打上「好」记号的拉丁动词，经法语传入英语。

items.en: Probus means 'good, upright', the adjective behind the testing verb.
items.cn: probus 意为「好的、正直的」，是那个检验动词背后的形容词。

items.en: Probare 'to test, prove' first meant to make or show something good.
items.cn: probare「检验、证明」最初意为使某物变好，或显示出它是好的。

items.en: Approbare 'to assent to' adds ad- to probare and gives the word its approving force.
items.cn: approbare「同意」在 probare 前加 ad-，赋予这个词认可的力量。

items.en: French aprover brings the verb to English, where it is recorded in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 法语 aprover 把这个动词带到英语，十四世纪已有记录。

items.en: The word now covers official permission and personal opinion alike.
items.cn: 这个词现在同时覆盖官方许可与个人意见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the approve family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of authorizing and accepting.
note.cn: 形近组收 approve 的词族；近义组收表示授权与接受的动词。

entries.definition: Showing a favourable opinion.
To judge something as wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「不赞成」，与 approve 相对。

entries.definition: To give formal power or permission for an action.
entries.definitionCN: 正式授予做某事的权力或许可，对应 approve 的批准义。

entries.definition: To give official approval, especially to a practice.
entries.definitionCN: 正式认可某项做法，语体偏正式。

entries.definition: To state public support for someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 公开表示支持某人某物，对应赞成义。

entries.definition: To agree to receive or take something.
entries.definitionCN: 同意接收或接受某物，范围比 approve 更宽。

normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子从官方印章走到私人点头。

normal.en: Probus is good; approve is showing that something is good.
normal.cn: probus 是好的；approve 就是表明某物是好的。

normal.en: A committee stamps a plan: official permission.
normal.cn: 委员会给方案盖印：正式批准。

normal.en: A parent nods at a choice: personal approval.
normal.cn: 父母对某个选择点头：私人认可。

abstract.cn: 同一个动词覆盖一份文件、一个选择、一个人与一件产品。

abstract.en: Every use asks whether something is good enough.
abstract.cn: 每个用法都在问：某物是否足够好。

abstract.en: Approving is a judgement that becomes an action.
abstract.cn: 批准是一个变成行动的评价。

examples.en: The committee voted to approve the new course in the spring.
examples.cn: 委员会投票通过了春季的新课程。

examples.en: Her parents do not approve of the late nights.
examples.cn: 她的父母不赞成她熬夜。

examples.cn: 这种药去年获批用于儿童。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普罗夫」——举着一枚写着可以的印章，往纸上盖：批准；赞成

root: approve 经古法语 aprover 来自拉丁语 approbare「同意、认可」，其形容词 probus 意为「好的、正直的」，动词 probare 意为检验并显示其好。整个词的底层动作是给某物打上「好」的记号：委员会给方案打记号就是正式批准，父母对选择打记号就是赞成，评选者给人打记号就是认可其适合，药监机构给药物打记号就是批准上市使用。

sensesIntro.en: Four uses give the mark of good to a plan, an opinion, a person, or a product.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个用法分别把「好」的记号盖在方案、意见、人与产品上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stamp reading good, pressed onto whatever is being judged.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚写着「好」的印章，盖在正被评判的东西上。

branches.en: THE OFFICE LINE: a body with authority stamps the plan.
branches.cn: 职权线：有权的机构给方案盖章。

branches.en: THE OPINION LINE: a private judgement gives the same stamp.
branches.cn: 意见线：私人的判断盖下同一枚印。

branches.en: THE PERSON LINE: a candidate is judged fit.
branches.cn: 人选线：候选人被判断为合适。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT LINE: the public may use it only after the stamp.
branches.cn: 产品线：盖印之后公众才能使用。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT LINE: authority and taste share one verb.
branches.cn: 评判线：职权与品味共用一个动词。

intro.en: Approve is a borrowed Latin verb whose suffix family is entirely regular.

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is real: probus 'good' and probare 'to test' are inside the verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁层是真实的：probus「好的」与 probare「检验」都在这个动词里。

definition_zh: 本金；主要的；校长；委托人
definition_en: the original sum of money borrowed; main or most important; a head teacher; one who authorises an agent
core_image: 一棵树干粗壮的大树，旁边摆着几张钞票，树上挂着写着小百分比的牌子
scene: 小李买房时向银行贷了一笔钱，还款表里第一项是本金，另一项是额外的费用。 He paid off the principal of his mortgage ten years early.
sceneCN: 这里 principal 指「贷款本金」（第 3 个义项：借款的原始金额）；句意为他提前十年还清了房贷的本金。图中可辨识物件：还款表格、树干代表的 principal、挂着的小牌子代表利息；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: main or primary
senses.definition: first in importance or rank
senses.definitionCN: 在重要性或地位上居于首位的
senses.example: The principal cause of the fire was faulty wiring.
senses.exampleCN: 火灾的主要原因是电线老化。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, direct from the Latin 'first, chief'.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，直接来自拉丁语「第一、首要」。

senses.title: head of a school
senses.definition: the head teacher of a school
senses.definitionCN: 一所学校的校长
senses.example: The principal gave a speech at graduation.
senses.exampleCN: 校长在毕业典礼上发表讲话。
senses.why: The head of an institution inherits the 'first, chief' sense.
senses.whyCN: 机构的负责人承接了「第一、首要」的意思。

senses.title: original sum lent
senses.definition: the amount of money originally borrowed, before interest is added
senses.definitionCN: 最初借来的金额，在加上利息之前
senses.example: Each monthly payment covers both principal and interest.
senses.exampleCN: 每月的还款既包括本金也包括利息。
senses.why: The original sum is the main part of the debt, separate from the interest that builds on it.
senses.whyCN: 原始金额是债务的主要部分，与在它之上累积的利息分开。

senses.title: party to a deal
senses.definition: a person for whom an agent acts in business or law
senses.definitionCN: 在商业或法律事务中由代理人代为行动的人
senses.example: As principal, she authorised her lawyer to sign the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 作为委托人，她授权律师代自己签合同。
senses.why: The one who authorises is the chief actor behind the agent.
senses.whyCN: 授权者是代理人背后的首要行为人。

senses.title: head of an embassy
senses.definition: the main diplomatic representative below an ambassador
senses.definitionCN: 低于大使级别的主要外交代表
senses.example: The embassy's principal met the foreign minister.
senses.exampleCN: 大使馆一等秘书拜会了外长。
senses.why: Another institutional 'first in rank' sense.
senses.whyCN: 另一种制度性的「首位」义。

senses.title: capital invested
senses.definition: money invested, as distinct from the income it produces
senses.definitionCN: 已投资的钱，与它产生的收益相区别
senses.example: The fund's principal remained intact through the downturn.
senses.exampleCN: 在衰退期间，基金的本金保持完好。
senses.why: The sum that sits underneath any return is the principal.
senses.whyCN: 任何收益之下的那笔钱就是 principal。

senses.title: main performer
senses.definition: the leading performer in a ballet, opera or similar
senses.definitionCN: 芭蕾、歌剧等中的主要演员
senses.example: The principal dancer fell ill before the curtain.
senses.exampleCN: 主演在开演前病倒了。
senses.why: Again the 'chief, first' sense applied to cast ranking.
senses.whyCN: 又是「首要、第一」义应用到演员排序上。

senses.title: main road
senses.definition: a main road, especially in the town or the principal artery
senses.definitionCN: 一条主要道路，尤指城镇里的主干道
senses.example: The principal road was closed for repairs.
senses.exampleCN: 那条主干道因维修封闭。
senses.why: A road that carries most traffic is the chief one.
senses.whyCN: 承载最多车流的路就是主干道。

intro.en: Principal and principle both descend from Latin princeps, but they split in meaning. Principal kept 'first in rank', principle took 'a rule'.
intro.cn: principal 与 principle 都来自拉丁语 princeps，但义分叉了。principal 保持「地位第一」，principle 则指「一条规则」。

items.en: Latin princeps meant 'first, chief'; it was built from primus 'first' + capere 'to take'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 princeps 意为「第一的、首要的」，由 primus「第一」+ capere「拿、取」构成。

items.en: Old French principal meant 'first' in the 12th century and passed into Middle English.
items.cn: 古法语 principal 在 12 世纪意为「第一的」，传入中古英语。

items.en: By the 14th century English principal meant 'chief person, head of a school', and by the 16th century the financial 'sum lent' appeared.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪英语 principal 已指「首要人物、校长」，到 16 世纪出现财务上「借出的金额」义。

items.en: Principle came through Latin principium 'beginning, rule'; it recorded the 'rule' sense that principal did not keep.
items.cn: principle 来自拉丁语 principium「起点、规则」，它承接了 principal 没有保持的「规则」义。

items.en: By the 19th century principal and interest became standard paired terms in loan documents.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，principal 与 interest 成为贷款文书里的固定配对术语。

items.en: Source solid: primus and capere are well documented. The split between principal and principle is a long-standing folk-etymology trap in English.
items.cn: 来源可靠：primus 与 capere 均有充分文献。principal 与 principle 的区分长期是英语使用者的陷阱。

note.en: Look-alikes are words with similar spelling; near meanings share the 'chief' or 'investment' territory.
note.cn: 形近是拼写相近的词；近义是与「首要」或「投资本金」领域邻近的词。

entries.definition: A basic truth or rule; not a person or a sum of money.
entries.definitionCN: 基本原则或规则；不指人也不指钱。

entries.definition: A male royal; shares the princeps root directly.
entries.definitionCN: 男性王室；直接共享 princeps 词根。

entries.definition: A female royal; from prince, same root but not identical.
entries.definitionCN: 女性王室；来自 prince，同根但不相同。

entries.tag: the fee that sits on principal
entries.definition: The money paid in addition to the principal on a loan.
entries.definitionCN: 在 principal 之上额外支付的钱。

entries.definition: Money used to generate income; broader than principal, which is the amount of a debt.
entries.definitionCN: 用来产生收益的钱；比 principal 宽，principal 特指债务的金额。

entries.definition: A chief person; principal is more formal for the role.
entries.definitionCN: 主要人物；principal 用于这个角色更正式。

entries.definition: A governing principle, but 'rule' is narrower than 'principle' (which is spelled -ple).
entries.definitionCN: 一条规则；但 rule 比 principle（拼 -ple 的那个）更窄。

normalIntro.en: Real morphemes, real relatives, real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 真实的构词、同族词和固定搭配。

normal.cn: principal 的根是 princeps，「第一、首要」义一直存在。

normal.cn: 固定配对：principal and interest。

normal.cn: primus「第一」还共享于 prime、primary、primitive。

normal.cn: capere「拿」还共享于 capture、captive、capability。

abstract.cn: 想象一棵树：树干是 principal，树枝是 interest。

abstract.cn: 想象全校集会，校长站在最前面。

abstract.cn: 想象一位拉丁语贵族说「我是第一」。

examples.en: Make extra payments to reduce the principal faster on your mortgage.
examples.cn: 额外还款可以更快地减少房贷的本金。

examples.en: The principal investigator led the team through three years of fieldwork.
examples.cn: 首席研究员带领团队完成了三年的实地工作。

examples.en: The principal's main objection was that the plan ignored local concerns.
examples.cn: 主要反对理由是该计划忽略了当地关切。

root: 拉丁语 princeps（primus「第一」+ capere「拿、取」）→ 古法语 principal → 英语 principal；与 principle（来自 principium「起点」）同源但义分叉。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from 'first, chief' → main → head of institution → sum lent (the chief part of a debt) → one behind an agent → embassy chief → investment capital → main performer → main road.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「第一、首要」向外辐射：主要的 → 机构负责人 → 借出的金额（债务的首要部分）→ 代理人背后的人 → 使馆主要官员 → 投资本金 → 主要演员 → 主要道路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tree trunk labelled PRINCIPAL with thin interest branches growing from it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根树干贴着 PRINCIPAL 标签，上面长着细小的 interest 树枝。

branches.en: THE CORE ADJECTIVE: chief, main, first in importance.
branches.cn: 核心形容词：首要的、主要的、第一的。

branches.en: INSTITUTIONAL HEADS AND MAIN THINGS: school, embassy, stage, road.
branches.cn: 机构负责人与主要事物：学校、使馆、舞台、道路。

branches.en: THE FINANCIAL CORE: the sum lent, separate from interest.
branches.cn: 财务核心：借出的金额，与 interest 相区分。

branches.en: INVESTMENT USE: capital invested, not income.
branches.cn: 投资用法：投入的本金，不是收益。

branches.en: THE LEGAL ACTOR: the one authorising an agent.
branches.cn: 法律行为者：授权代理人的那一方。

definition_zh: 渴望；愿望；想要
definition_en: a strong feeling of wanting something, or to want it strongly
core_image: 一只手隔着玻璃伸向柜台里的东西，指尖几乎碰到
scene: 孩子贴着玩具店的玻璃站着不动，母亲拉了两次也没拉动。 She felt a sudden desire to run out into the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 desire 指「渴望」（第 1 个义项：强烈地想要某物或做某事）；句意是她突然很想跑到雨里去。

senses.title: A strong pull toward something
senses.definition: a strong feeling of wanting to have something or to do something
senses.definitionCN: 想要得到某物或做某事的强烈感受
senses.example: She felt a sudden desire to run out into the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 她突然很想跑到雨里去。
senses.why: The body leans before the mind has finished arguing.
senses.whyCN: 心里还没争出结果，身体已经先倾过去了。

senses.title: Want it strongly
senses.definition: to want something strongly, especially in a formal or polite statement
senses.definitionCN: 强烈地想要某物，尤见于正式或客气的说法
senses.example: The committee desires a quick answer from the city.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会希望市里尽快给一个答复。
senses.why: The same pull becomes an action when it is spoken as a verb.
senses.whyCN: 同一股拉力一旦用动词说出来，就成了行动。

senses.title: The thing itself wished for
senses.definition: the particular thing that a person wishes to have
senses.definitionCN: 某人所希望得到的那样具体的东西
senses.example: Her one desire was a small house near the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 她唯一的心愿是海边的一座小房子。
senses.why: A feeling can harden into a single object the mind keeps pointing at.
senses.whyCN: 一种感受会凝固成一个具体的物件，让心思一直指着它。

intro.en: Desire comes from Latin desiderare, to long for, which Roman writers linked to de- and sidus, a star, as if waiting for a favourable sign.
intro.cn: desire 来自拉丁语 desiderare（渴望），罗马作家把它与 de- 和 sidus（星辰）相连，仿佛是等待一个吉兆。

items.en: Desiderare named the ache for something absent.
items.cn: desiderare 指对缺席之物的那种惦念。

items.en: The old guess was de- plus sidus, to stop looking at the stars and wait for one.
items.cn: 旧时的猜测是 de- 加 sidus，意为不再张望群星，只等那一颗。

items.en: Desirer carried the feeling into the language of court and prayer.
items.cn: desirer 把这股感受带进宫廷与祈祷的语言。

items.en: English used it for both holy longing and plain appetite.
items.cn: 英语用它兼指神圣的向往与普通的欲求。

items.en: It now covers everything from a wish for rain to a formal request.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖从盼一场雨到一份正式请求的一切。

note.en: The look-alike group all belong to the desire family, and the meaning group moves from quiet longing to sharp craving.
note.cn: 形近组都属于 desire 这一族，近义组则从安静的向往走到尖锐的渴求。

entries.definition: worth wanting
feeling a wish for something
not wanted at all
a deep and lasting wish
a very strong need for something
a hope for something to happen

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a hand pressed to shop glass and end with one small house by the sea.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一只手贴在商店玻璃上开始，落到海边的一座小房子。

normal.en: Desire is a hand that has already moved before permission arrives.
normal.cn: 渴望是一只手，许可还没到，它已经先动了。

normal.en: The old Romans heard a star inside the word.
normal.cn: 古罗马人从这个词里听见了一颗星。

normal.en: A wish can be quiet; a desire leans hard on the door.
normal.cn: 心愿可以很轻，渴望却会用力顶住那扇门。

normal.en: What you desire is often the shape your lack has taken.
normal.cn: 你所渴望的，常常就是你的缺失长成的形状。

normal.en: One desire, one object: the feeling narrows to a point.
normal.cn: 一种渴望，一个对象：感受收窄成一个点。

abstract.en: Picture a fingertip almost touching the glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一个指尖几乎贴到玻璃上。

abstract.en: Picture a small house with one lit window above the water.
abstract.cn: 想象水面上方一座亮着一扇窗的小房子。

abstract.en: Picture a star that will not come closer no matter how long you watch.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗无论看多久都不会靠近的星。

examples.en: She felt a sudden desire to run out into the rain.
examples.cn: 她突然很想跑到雨里去。

examples.en: The committee desires a quick answer from the city.
examples.cn: 委员会希望市里尽快给一个答复。

examples.en: Her one desire was a small house near the sea.
examples.cn: 她唯一的心愿是海边的一座小房子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 desire 记成「地摘尔」：de 向下，sire 像「伸手」，手一直往下伸，是想抓住渴望的东西。

root: 来自拉丁语 desiderare（渴望），由 de- 与 sidus（星辰）构成，古人把这份心情与等待吉星相连。本义是对缺席之物的惦念，后来兼指强烈的愿望、正式表达的想要，以及所盼望的那件具体东西。

sensesIntro.en: From a pull toward what is absent, to the act of wanting it aloud, to the one thing pointed at.
sensesIntro.cn: 从对缺席之物的牵引，到把想要说出口的动作，再到被指着的那一件东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching toward something behind glass.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸向玻璃后面的东西。

branches.en: The first sense is the pull itself, before any object is named.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是那股牵引本身，还没有点明对象。

branches.en: The second sense is the pull spoken aloud as a verb.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是把那股牵引用动词说出口。

branches.en: The third sense is the single thing at the end of the reach.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是伸出去的手最终指着的那件东西。

branches.en: Feeling and asking are the same force at two volumes.
branches.cn: 感受与请求，是同一种力道的一轻一重。

branches.en: To desire something is to let one object fill the whole view.
branches.cn: 想要某物，就是让一件东西占满整个视野。

intro.en: Desire gathers a family about wanting, from the quality of being worth wanting to the state of not being wanted.
intro.cn: desire 聚起一族表示「想要」的词，从值得想要的性质到不被想要的状态。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin desiderare, to long for, and the family adds endings for quality, manner and negation.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是拉丁语 desiderare（渴望），这一族用后缀添上性质、方式与否定。

items.example: He had no desire to argue.
Those desiring tickets should write in.

items.meaning: full of a wish for something

items.exampleCN: 这项变动带来了不想要的成本。

definition_zh: 要求；必要条件；规定
definition_en: something that is needed or officially demanded before something else can happen
core_image: 入学通知书背后列着一串必须满足的条件，逐条打钩才能注册
scene: 报名表背面列着语言成绩、体检证明等多项要求，缺一项就无法注册。 The entrance requirement includes a health certificate.
sceneCN: 这里 requirement 是「要求；必要条件」（第 1 个义项：必须满足的条件）；句意：入学要求包括一份健康证明。

senses.title: Something that is needed
senses.definition: a thing that is necessary for something to happen or be achieved
senses.definitionCN: 某事发生或达成所必需的东西
senses.example: A good camera is a basic requirement for the course.
senses.exampleCN: 一台好相机是这门课程的基本要求。
senses.why: The noun names what the verb require points to: the need that must be met.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词指 require 所指向的东西：必须被满足的需要。

senses.title: An official rule or demand
senses.definition: an official condition set by an authority
senses.definitionCN: 由权威机构设定的正式条件
senses.example: The building meets all safety requirements.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋建筑符合所有安全规定。
senses.why: When a need is written into a rule, it becomes a requirement in the official sense.
senses.whyCN: 当需要被写进规则，它就成为正式意义上的「要求」。

senses.title: The act of requiring
senses.definition: the act of demanding something formally
senses.definitionCN: 正式提出要求的动作
senses.example: The requirement of a deposit surprised the tenants.
senses.exampleCN: 要求交押金让租客们吃了一惊。
senses.why: The -ment ending can still name the action itself, not only its content.
senses.whyCN: -ment 词尾仍可指动作本身，而不只是动作的内容。

intro.en: Requirement is require plus the noun ending -ment, naming a needed condition or the act of demanding it.
intro.cn: requirement 是 require 加名词词尾 -ment，指必需的条件或提出要求的动作。

items.en: Quaerere means to seek, and requirere means to seek again.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻求，requirere 意为再次寻求。

items.en: Old French requerre brings the demand sense into English require.
items.cn: 古法语 requerre 把「要求」义带进英语 require。

items.en: Middle English require covers need and obligation.
items.cn: 中古英语 require 涵盖需要与义务。

items.en: The noun requirement appears for a condition that must be met.
items.cn: 名词 requirement 出现，指必须满足的条件。

items.en: Education and engineering spread requirements in rules and specifications.
items.cn: 教育与工程使 requirements 广泛用于规则和规格说明。

items.en: Modern English uses it for entry rules, legal conditions, and design needs.
items.cn: 现代英语用它表示入学规则、法律条件和设计需求。

note.en: Requirement is the noun of require, and it is close to words for conditions that must be satisfied.
note.cn: requirement 是 require 的名词，与表示必须满足的条件的词相邻。

necessary for a purpose
an official demand for supplies
something that is needed

normalIntro.en: Requirement is require plus -ment, so it is the thing a need or rule requires you to have.
normalIntro.cn: requirement 是 require 加 -ment，指需要或规则要求你具备的东西。

normal.en: Require plus -ment: the condition that must be met.
normal.cn: require 加 -ment：必须被满足的条件。

normal.en: Meet the requirements is the phrase for satisfying every condition.
normal.cn: meet the requirements 意为满足所有条件。

normal.en: Entry requirements are what a school asks for before you can join.
normal.cn: entry requirements 是学校在你入学前提出的条件。

normal.en: A legal requirement is a condition written into law.
normal.cn: legal requirement 是写进法律的条件。

normal.en: The minimum requirement is the lowest condition still accepted.
normal.cn: minimum requirement 是仍被接受的最低条件。

abstract.en: Picture a checklist on the back of an admission letter, each box waiting for a tick.
abstract.cn: 想象入学通知书背面有一张清单，每个方框都等着打钩。

abstract.en: Imagine a doorway with a height bar that everyone must pass under.
abstract.cn: 想象门口有一根横杆，所有人都必须从下面通过。

abstract.en: Think of a recipe card listing what must be in the kitchen first.
abstract.cn: 想象一张食谱卡，先列出厨房里必须准备好的东西。

examples.en: The job has three basic requirements.
examples.cn: 这份工作有三项基本要求。

examples.en: All new buildings must meet fire safety requirements.
examples.cn: 所有新建筑都必须符合消防安全规定。

examples.en: Experience is a requirement for this position.
examples.cn: 经验是这个职位的必备条件。

dict_mnemonic.text: require（需要、要求）+ -ment（名词词尾）＝要求或必要条件；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: require（需要、要求，源自拉丁语 requirere「再次寻求」）+ 名词词尾 -ment，指必须满足的条件或提出要求的行为。

sensesIntro.en: A needed thing comes first, then the official rule that demands it, then the act of demanding itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是必需之物，再是要求它的正式规则，最后是提出要求的行为本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a condition that must be ticked before the next step is allowed.
core.cn: 核心意象：必须打钩才能进入下一步的条件。

branches.en: The necessary thing is the basic sense of the noun.
branches.cn: 必需之物，是这个名词的基本义项。

branches.en: An official rule turns a need into a written condition.
branches.cn: 正式规则把需要变成书面条件。

branches.en: The noun can still name the act of demanding.
branches.cn: 这个名词仍可指提出要求的动作。

branches.en: Personal needs and official rules both set a bar to clear.
branches.cn: 个人需要与官方规则都设下一道必须跨过的门槛。

branches.en: The written rule and the act of demanding it are two sides of one condition.
branches.cn: 书面规则与提出要求的动作，是同一个条件的两面。

intro.en: Requirement is a transparent English noun: require plus the ending -ment.
intro.cn: requirement 是构词透明的英语名词：require 加词尾 -ment。

latinIntro.en: The base require comes from Latin requirere, to seek again, and -ment marks the action or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 基础词 require 来自拉丁语 requirere（再次寻求），-ment 标记动作或其结果。

items.example: Require is the base of requirement.
items.exampleCN: require 是 requirement 的基础词。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾

items.exampleCN: requirement 由 require 与 -ment 合成。

items.example: Requisite shares the Latin seek root.
items.exampleCN: requisite 共享拉丁「寻求」词根。

items.example: Requisition shares the same Latin source.
items.exampleCN: requisition 共享同一拉丁来源。
re- 出现在 require 词干开头。

items.example: Quaerere is the deepest root of requirement.
items.exampleCN: quaerere 是 requirement 最深的词根。

definition_zh: 神经；勇气；胆量；放肆；紧张不安；鼓起勇气
definition_en: a fibre that carries signals in the body; courage to do something difficult; bold rudeness; a state of nervous tension; to give oneself courage
core_image: 一根细长的白线从脊柱伸向指尖，轻轻一碰就传来一阵电流
scene: 冬天的早晨，厨房的水壶在响，母亲搓着手站在门口，声音有些发抖。 I did not have the nerve to tell her the truth.
sceneCN: 这里是「胆量、勇气」（第 2 个义项：做难事所需的胆量）；句意为我没有勇气把实情告诉她。图中可辨识物件：冒着热气的水壶、门口的双手。

pos.zh: 神经；勇气；胆量；放肆；紧张不安

derivatives.zh: 由 nerve 加 -ous 构成，义为「紧张的；神经的」
由 nervous 加 -ly 构成，义为「紧张地；不安地」
由 nervous 加 -ness 构成，义为「紧张；神经质」
由拉丁前缀 e-（去掉）加 nervus 构成，义为「使失去活力」

senses.title: A fibre carrying signals between the brain and the body
senses.definition: a long fibre in the body that carries messages between the brain, the senses and the muscles
senses.definitionCN: 体内传递信息的长纤维，连接大脑、感官与肌肉
senses.example: The dentist damaged a nerve in my jaw.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医伤到了我下颌的一根神经。
senses.why: Latin nervus first named a sinew or tendon, the visible white cord in a body; anatomists then gave that same cord the job of carrying feeling, and the word kept the picture of a thread running through flesh.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nervus 最初指筋或肌腱，也就是身体里看得见的白色细索；解剖学家随后让这同一根索承担传递感觉的职责，这个词便保留了「细线穿过血肉」的画面。

senses.title: Courage to face something difficult
senses.definition: the steady confidence needed to do something frightening or demanding
senses.definitionCN: 面对可怕或艰难之事时所需的稳定信心
senses.example: The climber finally lost his nerve near the summit.
senses.exampleCN: 那名登山者在接近山顶时终于失去了勇气。
senses.why: Sinews are what keep a body taut and steady, so to have nerve came to mean to hold that taut strength when fear pulls at it; courage is the sinew of the mind.
senses.whyCN: 筋让身体绷紧、稳住，因此 to have nerve 就指在恐惧拉扯时仍保持那种绷紧的力量；勇气成了心智的筋。

senses.title: Bold impudence that ignores what others expect
senses.definition: rude boldness shown by doing something others consider too cheeky
senses.definitionCN: 做出别人认为太冒失的事而显出的无礼大胆
senses.example: He had the nerve to ask for a second raise.
senses.exampleCN: 他竟厚着脸皮要求再加一次薪。
senses.why: The same strength that deserves praise can also be judged as bare-faced boldness when it ignores other people's feelings, so a word for taut power slides into a word for cheek.
senses.whyCN: 同一种值得称赞的力量，一旦无视别人的感受，也会被判为赤裸裸的放肆；于是表示「绷紧之力」的词滑成了表示「厚脸皮」的词。

senses.title: A state of nervous tension, usually in the plural
senses.definition: a feeling of being anxious and unable to relax, commonly used as the plural nerves
senses.definitionCN: 焦虑、无法放松的感觉，常用复数形式
senses.example: She had a bad case of nerves before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试之前她紧张得厉害。
senses.why: Nerves were understood as the body's sensitive cords, so when those cords were overexcited the name moved from the fibres to the feeling they produced; a case of nerves is the body reporting on itself.
senses.whyCN: nerves 被理解为身体里敏感的细索，当这些索过度兴奋时，名称就从纤维转到它们产生的感觉；a case of nerves 就是身体在报告自己的状态。

senses.title: To give oneself or another person courage
senses.definition: to make oneself or someone else brave enough to do something difficult
senses.definitionCN: 使自己或别人有足够勇气去做难事
senses.example: He nerved himself to knock on the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他鼓起勇气去敲门。
senses.why: Turning the noun into a verb makes courage into a supply that can be gathered and handed over; the word changes from a thing felt in the chest to an act performed before a door.
senses.whyCN: 把名词变成动词，勇气就成了一种可以聚拢、可以递送的东西；这个词从胸腔里感到的状态，变成门前做出的动作。

intro.en: Nerve began as a Latin word for a sinew, and English stretched that cord from anatomy to courage and then to cheek, finally turning it into a verb.
intro.cn: nerve 起初是拉丁语中表示「筋」的词，英语把这条索从解剖拉到勇气、再到厚脸皮，最后还把它变成动词。

items.en: Nervus meant a sinew, tendon or cord, and Roman writers already used it for the cords running inside the body.
items.cn: nervus 意为筋、肌腱或细索，古罗马作者已用它指体内穿行的索状结构。

items.en: The adjective nervosus described something sinewy, strong and vigorous, and it is the ancestor of the English word for being tense.
items.cn: 形容词 nervosus 描述充满筋腱、强壮有力的事物，是英语中表示「紧张」那个词的祖先。

items.en: Old French nerf named a nerve or sinew and passed the word to English in the medieval period.
items.cn: 古法语 nerf 指神经或筋，在中世纪把这个词传入英语。

items.en: Middle English nerve kept the anatomical sense, while the idea of bodily strength slowly became the idea of mental courage.
items.cn: 中古英语 nerve 保留了解剖义，而「身体有力」的观念慢慢变成了「精神有胆量」。

items.en: Modern English adds the plural sense of tension, the verb of gathering courage, and the judgemental sense of bold impudence.
items.cn: 现代英语添上复数的「紧张不安」义、聚拢勇气的动词义，以及带评判意味的「放肆」义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adjectives, adverbs and verbs built on the Latin cord; the near-meaning group holds words for steadiness, boldness and the body's tough tissue.
note.cn: 形近组收建在拉丁语「索」上的形容词、副词与动词；近义组收表示镇定、大胆以及身体坚韧组织的词。

entries.definition: Anxious or easily worried; also relating to the nerves.
entries.definitionCN: 焦虑、易担忧的；也与神经有关。

entries.definition: In an anxious or fidgety manner, formed with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 以焦虑或坐立不安的方式；由 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The state of being anxious, formed with -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 焦虑、紧张的状态；由 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: To weaken or drain energy, from Latin e- plus nervus.
entries.definitionCN: 使虚弱、失去活力；来自拉丁语 e- 加 nervus。

entries.definition: The ability to face danger or pain without being stopped by fear.
entries.definitionCN: 面对危险或痛苦而不被恐惧挡住的能力。

entries.definition: Bold determination in a difficult situation, used in lively speech.
entries.definitionCN: 在困境中的大胆决心，多用于口语。

entries.definition: Bold and rude confidence that shocks other people.
entries.definitionCN: 大胆无礼、令旁人吃惊的自信。

entries.definition: A tendon or tough cord of tissue, the original bodily image of nerve.
entries.definitionCN: 肌腱或坚韧的索状组织，是 nerve 最初的身体意象。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin cord of sinew that English turned into a metaphor for courage, and its family keeps both the fibre and the feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中一根筋索，英语把它变成勇气的比喻，同族词同时保留纤维与感觉两面。

normal.en: Latin nervus meant sinew or tendon, and the anatomists simply extended that visible cord to the fibres that carry feeling.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nervus 指筋或肌腱，解剖学家只是把这条看得见的索扩展到传递感觉的纤维。

normal.en: Nervous adds -ous to nerve, so it first meant full of sinew and therefore strong, not anxious.
normal.cn: nervous 是 nerve 加 -ous，最初意为「充满筋腱」因而强壮，而不是焦虑。

normal.en: To have the nerve connects courage to the tautness of sinew: a steady body is the picture behind a steady will.
normal.cn: to have the nerve 把勇气与筋的绷紧连起来：稳定的身体正是稳定意志的画面。

normal.en: The plural nerves names the fibres and also the feeling of tension, which is why a case of nerves sounds both medical and emotional.
normal.cn: 复数 nerves 既指纤维，也指紧张的感觉，所以 a case of nerves 听起来既像医学说法又像情绪描述。

normal.en: Nerve as a verb is the noun put to work: to nerve oneself is to gather the taut strength and hold it before acting.
normal.cn: nerve 作动词是名词被派去干活：to nerve oneself 就是聚起那股绷紧的力量，在行动前稳住它。

abstract.en: A word for a physical cord becomes a word for moral steadiness, because courage feels like something pulled tight in the chest.
abstract.cn: 一个指身体细索的词变成了指精神稳定的词，因为勇气感觉像胸腔里有什么被拉紧了。

abstract.en: The distance from courage to cheek is short: both are strength that refuses to be held back by other people's expectations.
abstract.cn: 从勇气到厚脸皮只隔一小步：两者都是不肯被旁人期待挡回去的力量。

abstract.en: Nerve can be a fibre, a feeling, a virtue, an insult and an action, which shows how far one bodily image can travel.
abstract.cn: nerve 可以是纤维、感觉、美德、骂人的话，也可以是一个动作，可见一个身体意象能走多远。

examples.en: A damaged nerve can take months to heal.
examples.cn: 受损的神经可能需要几个月才能愈合。

examples.en: She lost her nerve and stepped back from the edge.
examples.cn: 她失去了勇气，从边缘退了回来。

examples.en: He nerved himself to open the letter.
examples.cn: 他鼓起勇气拆开了那封信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呢夫」——神经绷得像一根细线，人也跟着紧张起来；nerve 就是神经、勇气。

root: 拉丁语 nervus（筋、肌腱、神经）经古法语 nerf 进入英语；一般认为与希腊语 neuron（筋、神经）同源，同族词有 nervous、nervously、enervate 等。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a taut cord in the body; anatomy supplies the fibre, and the tautness supplies courage, cheek, tension and the act of steeling oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是身体里一根绷紧的索；解剖提供纤维义，绷紧感则提供勇气、厚脸皮、紧张不安与鼓劲这几个义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin white cord running from the spine to a fingertip, carrying a small electric pulse when touched.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细白索从脊柱伸到指尖，被触碰时传过一小阵电流。

branches.en: a nerve cell seen under a microscope
branches.cn: 显微镜下的一枚神经细胞

branches.en: a dentist numbing one side of the jaw
branches.cn: 牙医让半边下颌失去知觉

branches.en: a climber hesitating near the summit
branches.cn: 接近山顶时犹豫的登山者

branches.en: a second request that shocks the room
branches.cn: 让满屋人吃惊的第二次请求

branches.en: a waiting room full of shallow breathing
branches.cn: 满是浅促呼吸的候诊室

intro.en: The word is a Latin noun for sinew, its adjective of strength, the French form that carried it, and the English words that grew from the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示「筋」的名词、表示强壮的形容词、承载它的法语形式，以及同一词干上的英语词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplied the noun for sinew and the adjective for strength, and French passed the noun to English before the metaphor of courage developed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「筋」的名词与「强壮」的形容词，法语把名词传给英语，之后才发展出勇气的比喻。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of

definition_zh: 亲自；本人；就个人而言；针对个人地；以个人身份
definition_en: in your own person rather than through someone else, or as your own opinion
core_image: 一个人把袖口挽起，自己伸手去搬那只箱子，不叫别人代劳
scene: 会议开到一半，负责人放下笔，环视一圈，表示这件事他要自己去做，不转交别人。 I will personally check every page before it goes out.
sceneCN: 这里是「亲自、本人」（第 1 个义项：不假手他人，由当事人自己做）；句意为每一页在发出去之前他都要亲自核对。画面里是他卷起袖子自己动手的样子。

pos.zh: 亲自；本人；就个人而言；针对个人地

derivatives.zh: 去掉副词后缀 -ly 得到的形容词，义为「个人的；私人的」
同族名词，来自拉丁语 persona，义为「人」
由否定前缀 im- 加 personal 构成，义为「非个人的；没有人情味的」

senses.title: In your own person, not through another
senses.definition: done by you yourself rather than by someone acting for you
senses.definitionCN: 由你本人去做，而不是由替你办事的人去做
senses.example: The manager personally handed each worker a letter.
senses.exampleCN: 经理亲自把信交到每位工人手里。
senses.why: The adverb simply turns the adjective into a manner: in the manner of the person himself, with no stand-in in between.
senses.whyCN: 副词只是把形容词变成方式状语：以本人的方式去做，中间不隔一个代办的人。

senses.title: As my own opinion
senses.definition: used to mark a statement as your own view rather than as a general fact
senses.definitionCN: 用来表明某句话只是你自己的看法，而不是普遍事实
senses.example: Personally, I would wait another week before deciding.
senses.exampleCN: 就我个人而言，我会再等一周才作决定。
senses.why: If the word points to the speaker in person, it can also point to that speaker's private judgement as against what everyone says.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词指向说话人本人，它也能指向这个人自己的判断，与大家普遍的说法相对，于是有了发表私见的用法。

senses.title: As an attack on oneself
senses.definition: in a way that feels aimed at you as a person rather than at what you did
senses.definitionCN: 以一种让人感到是冲着你这个人、而不是针对你所做之事的方式
senses.example: She took the criticism personally and stopped speaking to us.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那句批评当成了针对自己，从此不再和我们说话。
senses.why: To take something personally is to move the remark from the work to the worker, and the adverb marks exactly that shift.
senses.whyCN: 把一句话当成针对个人，就是把评价从事情挪到人身上，副词正是标明这一挪动发生在哪里。

senses.title: As an individual, in one's own right
senses.definition: in your own individual capacity, especially when responsibility or blame is assigned
senses.definitionCN: 以你个人的身份，尤用于责任或过失的归属
senses.example: He is personally liable for the damage caused by the machine.
senses.exampleCN: 他对这台机器造成的损失负有个人责任。
senses.why: Legal and official writing needs to separate a role from the person filling it, so the adverb pins responsibility on the individual body.
senses.whyCN: 法律与公文需要把职位和坐在职位上的人分开，副词就把责任钉在具体这个人身上。

intro.en: Personally is an English formation: the adjective personal, itself from Latin persona, plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: personally 是英语自己构成的词：形容词 personal（源自拉丁语 persona）加上副词词尾 -ly。

items.en: Persona meant a mask and the role it marked; its earlier origin is uncertain.
items.cn: persona 意为面具以及面具所标示的角色；它更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Late Latin personalis meant belonging to a person and reached English through French as personal.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 personalis 意为属于某个人的，经法语以 personal 的形式进入英语。

items.en: Middle English had the adjective personal but no settled adverb, and writers used phrases such as in person instead.
items.cn: 中古英语已有形容词 personal，却没有定型的副词，人们多用「以本人身份」一类短语。

items.en: Adding the native suffix -ly to personal produced personally, following the usual adjective-to-adverb pattern.
items.cn: 在 personal 后加英语本族后缀 -ly，按形容词变副词的常规路子构成了 personally。

items.en: By the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries personally also marks a speaker's own opinion and, in law, individual liability.
items.cn: 到十八、十九世纪，personally 又用来标记说话人自己的看法，并在法律中指个人责任。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun and adjective this adverb was built from; the near-meaning group collects words for doing something oneself.
note.cn: 形近组收构成这个副词的名词与形容词；近义组收表示本人亲自做某事的词。

entries.definition: The adjective the adverb was built from, meaning of one person or private.
entries.definitionCN: 构成这个副词的原形容词，意为个人的或私人的。

entries.definition: A single human being, the noun at the bottom of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 一个单独的人，是这一族词最底层的名词。

entries.definition: The qualities that make one person different from another.
entries.definitionCN: 使一个人区别于他人的那些特质。

entries.definition: In a way that shows no feeling for the individual involved.
entries.definitionCN: 以不关心具体某个人的方式。

entries.definition: Present yourself rather than sending someone or something.
entries.definitionCN: 本人到场，而不是派人或送东西去。

entries.definition: Without any person or thing in between.
entries.definitionCN: 中间不经过任何人和物。

entries.definition: Used to stress that a person acts without help.
entries.definitionCN: 用来强调某人无需他人帮助地行动。

entries.definition: In a way that is not public and not shared.
entries.definitionCN: 以不公开、不与人分享的方式。

normalIntro.en: The adverb is personal plus a native ending, and it keeps the whole range of the noun person inside one word.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词就是 personal 加一个本族词尾，把「人」这个名词的全部跨度收进了一个词里。

normal.en: Personally is personal plus -ly, the ordinary English way of turning an adjective into an adverb of manner.
normal.cn: personally 就是 personal 加 -ly，是英语把形容词变成方式副词最普通的方式。

normal.en: The same ending that gives personally also gives quickly, so the pattern carries over without effort.
normal.cn: 构成 personally 的这个词尾也能构成 quickly，所以这个模式可以毫不费力地套用。

normal.en: In person and personally both stress the body of the person, but only the adverb can also mean in my opinion.
normal.cn: in person 与 personally 都强调本人的身体，但只有副词还能表示在我看来。

normal.en: Take it personally is almost always negative: the remark was about the work, and the listener heard it about the self.
normal.cn: 把它当成针对自己几乎总是负面的：话本来说的是工作，听的人却听成了说自己。

normal.en: In contracts, personally liable fixes blame on the human being behind the company name.
normal.cn: 在合同里，负有个人责任把责任固定在公司名号背后的那个真人身上。

abstract.en: A mask becomes an adverb: the word now describes how a person steps forward in his own body.
abstract.cn: 面具变成了副词：这个词现在描述一个人如何以自己的肉身站出来。

abstract.en: Personally is a small flag planted on a sentence to show that one particular speaker is standing behind it.
abstract.cn: personally 是插在句子上的一面小旗，表明有某一个具体的说话人站在它后面。

abstract.en: The distance between a rule and the person it hits is exactly the space this adverb measures.
abstract.cn: 规则与它所击中的人之间的距离，正是这个副词丈量的空间。

examples.en: The chef personally tasted every dish before service.
examples.cn: 上菜之前，主厨亲自尝了每一道菜。

examples.en: Personally, I think the plan is too risky.
examples.cn: 就我个人而言，我觉得这个计划风险太大。

examples.en: Please do not take this personally, but your report needs more evidence.
examples.cn: 请别把这话当成针对你，不过你的报告还需要更多证据。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼森呢哩」——破伞的人宁可自己淋雨，也要亲自把伞递到你手上；personally 就是亲自。

root: 拉丁语 persona（面具、角色）构成 personalis，再进入英语成为形容词 personal，加 -ly 得到 personally；核心始终是某一个具体的人。

sensesIntro.en: The adverb keeps the noun of person alive: it can mean the body that acts, the mind that judges, the target of an insult, or the name on a legal duty.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个副词始终活在「人」这个名词里：它可以指动手的身体、下判断的头脑、被冒犯的对象，也可以指法律责任上的那个名字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching past an offered helper and lifting the box by itself.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人把袖口挽起，越过别人伸来的手，自己把箱子搬起来。

branches.en: a manager handing out letters one by one
branches.cn: 经理一封一封把信递出去

branches.en: a raised hand before an opinion is given
branches.cn: 给出看法之前先举起一只手

branches.en: a remark that lands on the wrong target
branches.cn: 一句话落到了错的目标上

branches.en: a signature under a clause about damage
branches.cn: 损失条款下方的一个签名

branches.en: the same voice saying I did it and I think so
branches.cn: 同一个声音说「我做的」和「我认为」

intro.en: The adverb is a chain of three built pieces: a Latin noun, a Latin adjective ending and a native adverb ending.
intro.cn: 这个副词是三段构造成果串起来的：一个拉丁名词、一个拉丁形容词词尾，一个本族副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Only the noun and the adjective are Latin; the adverb itself was assembled inside English with a native ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语只提供了那个名词和形容词；副词本身是英语用本族词尾自行拼起来的。

definition_zh: 商品；货物；动产
definition_en: things made or bought for sale, or movable property in law
core_image: 仓库里堆满贴着标签的纸箱，叉车正把一箱箱货物运上货车
scene: 货车把货物运到仓库。 The truck carried goods to the warehouse.
sceneCN: 这里 goods 是「商品、货物」（第 1 个义项）；句意：货车把货物运到仓库。

senses.title: Things for sale
senses.definition: things that are made or bought to be sold or used
senses.definitionCN: 为出售或使用而制造或购买的东西
senses.example: The truck carried goods to the warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 货车把货物运到仓库。
senses.why: This is the everyday trading sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词日常的商业含义。

senses.title: Movable property
senses.definition: property that can be moved, as opposed to land, in law
senses.definitionCN: 法律上与土地相对、可以移动的财产
senses.example: The court divided the goods between the two heirs.
senses.exampleCN: 法院把动产分给了两位继承人。
senses.why: The old legal sense still survives in contracts and courts.
senses.whyCN: 这一古老的法律义在合同和法庭中仍然存在。

senses.title: Exactly what is wanted
senses.definition: the thing that is needed or promised, used informally
senses.definitionCN: 所需要或所承诺的东西，用于口语
senses.example: Her new album really delivers the goods.
senses.exampleCN: 她的新专辑确实不负所望。
senses.why: Informal speech uses the goods for what someone actually wants.
senses.whyCN: 口语用 the goods 表示人们真正想要的东西。

intro.en: Goods began as good things, then narrowed to things for trade.
intro.cn: goods 最初指「好东西」，后来收窄为用于交易的货物。

items.en: God meant good, and goods meant good things.
items.cn: god 意为好的，goods 意为好东西。

items.en: Goodes came to mean property and possessions.
items.cn: goodes 逐渐表示财产和所有物。

items.en: Goods narrowed to wares offered in trade.
items.cn: goods 收窄为市场上出售的商品。

items.en: Economists paired it with services.
items.cn: 经济学家把它与服务并列。

items.en: The old legal sense of movable property survived.
items.cn: 表示动产的古老法律义保留了下来。

note.en: Goods is compared with look-alike words and words for traded things.
note.cn: 把 goods 与形近词以及表示交易物的词作比较。

entries.definition: a large water bird
a precious yellow metal
a being worshipped
goods for sale
goods carried by ship or plane
small goods offered for sale

normalIntro.en: Goods is the plural of good things turned into things for trade.
normalIntro.cn: goods 是「好东西」的复数，后来变成用来交易的货物。

normal.en: The truck carried goods to the warehouse.
normal.cn: 货车把货物运到仓库。

normal.en: The shop sells electrical goods.
normal.cn: 这家店出售电器商品。

normal.en: Goods and services are both part of trade.
normal.cn: 商品与服务都是贸易的一部分。

normal.en: The police found the stolen goods.
normal.cn: 警方找到了赃物。

normal.en: Her new album really delivers the goods.
normal.cn: 她的新专辑确实不负所望。

abstract.en: Goods move where money calls them.
abstract.cn: 货物往金钱呼唤的地方流动。

abstract.en: A thing becomes goods when hands begin to trade it.
abstract.cn: 当双手开始交易，东西就成了货物。

abstract.en: The worth of goods is a story told by the market.
abstract.cn: 货物的价值，是市场讲述的故事。

examples.en: The truck carried goods to the warehouse.
examples.cn: 货车把货物运到仓库。

examples.en: The court divided the goods between the two heirs.
examples.cn: 法院把动产分给了两位继承人。

examples.en: Her new album really delivers the goods.
examples.cn: 她的新专辑确实不负所望。

dict_mnemonic.text: goods 是 good（好的）的复数形式演变而来的名词，指「商品、货物」；consumer goods 是「消费品」，goods and services 是「商品与服务」，stolen goods 是「赃物」，deliver the goods 是「兑现承诺」。

root: 来自古英语 gōd（好的、财物），复数 goods 原指「好东西、财物」，后专指用于买卖的商品以及法律上的动产。

sensesIntro.en: Goods means things for sale, movable property in law, or informally exactly what is wanted.
sensesIntro.cn: goods 指出售的商品、法律上的动产，或口语中真正需要的东西。

core.en: Things that carry value and can be exchanged.
core.cn: 承载价值、可供交换的东西。

branches.en: Boxes leave a warehouse on a truck.
branches.cn: 纸箱被装上货车离开仓库。

branches.en: A court lists furniture and shares it out.
branches.cn: 法庭列出家具并加以分配。

branches.en: An album finally proves it was worth waiting for.
branches.cn: 一张专辑终于证明值得等待。

branches.en: Traded wares and movable property are both owned things.
branches.cn: 交易的商品与动产，都是被拥有的东西。

branches.en: A promise kept and a product sold are both delivered goods.
branches.cn: 兑现的承诺与售出的产品，都是交付的「货」。

intro.en: Goods connects to the good family of words.
intro.cn: goods 与 good 这个词族相连。

latinIntro.en: Goods is Germanic and has no Latin root.
latinIntro.cn: goods 属日耳曼语，没有拉丁词根。

items.example: The truck carried goods to the warehouse.
She is known for her goodness.
The gift was a sign of goodwill.
items.exampleCN: 这份礼物是善意的表示。

items.example: The bag was full of goodies.
items.exampleCN: 袋子里装满了好吃的东西。

items.example: The child asked for a goody.

definition_zh: 装置；设备；手段；手法
definition_en: a machine or tool made for a particular purpose
core_image: 桌上一个拆开的小机器，线圈和齿轮裸露在外
scene: 他拧开外壳，里面的线圈和齿轮露出来，桌上散着小螺丝。 The device measures the moisture in the soil.
sceneCN: 这里 device 指「装置」（第 1 个义项：为特定用途做的小机器）；句意是这个装置测量土壤里的湿度。

senses.title: A piece of equipment
senses.definition: a machine or tool made for a particular job
senses.definitionCN: 为某项特定工作而制造的机器或工具
senses.example: The device measures the moisture in the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 这个装置测量土壤里的湿度。
senses.why: Human hands cannot stay in the field all year, so a small machine does.
senses.whyCN: 人的手没法整年守在田里，于是让一台小机器守着。

senses.title: A method or trick
senses.definition: a plan or trick used to get a particular result
senses.definitionCN: 为得到某个结果而用的计策或花招
senses.example: Silence was just a device to make us talk.
senses.exampleCN: 沉默只是一种让我们开口的手段。
senses.why: A plan can work like a tool even when it has no parts.
senses.whyCN: 一个计策即使没有零件，也能像工具那样起作用。

senses.title: A literary technique
senses.definition: a particular way of writing that produces a chosen effect
senses.definitionCN: 为产生某种效果而采用的特定写法
senses.example: The writer uses repetition as a poetic device.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作家把重复当作一种诗歌手法。
senses.why: Words can be arranged as carefully as gears.
senses.whyCN: 词语也能像齿轮那样被仔细排布。

intro.en: Device comes from Old French devis, a plan or division, which grew from Latin dividere, to divide, and it split from the verb devise.
intro.cn: device 来自古法语 devis（计划、划分），源头是拉丁语 dividere（分开），后来与动词 devise 分了家。

items.en: Dividere meant to divide or separate a whole into parts.
items.cn: dividere 指把一个整体分开、切成几部分。

items.en: Devis named a plan, a division of work or a design.
items.cn: devis 指一份计划、一种分工或一个设计。

items.en: English device first meant a plan or a heraldic design.
items.cn: 英语 device 最初指计划或纹章图案。

items.en: The sense shifted from the plan to the thing built from it.
items.cn: 词义从计划本身转到了照计划造出来的东西。

items.en: It now means any small machine, and also a trick or a method.
items.cn: 如今它指任何小型机器，也指花招或方法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vis shape, while the meaning group names useful objects and tools.
note.cn: 形近组共用 vis 这一段，近义组则给出有用的小物件与工具。

entries.definition: to invent a plan or a method
not direct or honest
an opinion about what someone should do
entries.definitionCN: 关于某人该怎么做的一种意见

entries.definition: a small useful machine
a tool used for careful work
an object held to do a job

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a cracked-open casing on a table and end with a writer counting repeated words.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从桌上一个撬开的外壳开始，落到一位反复数词的作家。

normal.en: A device begins as a devis, a plan drawn before any part exists.
normal.cn: device 起初只是一个 devis，一张还没有零件时就画好的图。

normal.en: Take one letter away and the noun becomes the verb devise.
normal.cn: 拿掉一个字母，名词就变成动词 devise。

normal.en: Anything with a switch can be called a device today.
normal.cn: 今天任何带开关的东西都能叫 device。

normal.en: Silence can be a device too, with no wires at all.
normal.cn: 沉默也能是一种手段，一根线都不用。

normal.en: A repeated phrase is a device the ear remembers.
normal.cn: 重复的句子是一种耳朵记得住的手法。

abstract.en: Picture a screwdriver beside four loose screws.
abstract.cn: 想象一把螺丝刀旁边放着四颗松开的螺丝。

abstract.en: Picture a blue light blinking on a small plastic box.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小塑料盒上闪着蓝灯。

abstract.en: Picture the same word printed five times down a page.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个词在纸上竖着印了五遍。

examples.en: The device measures the moisture in the soil.
examples.cn: 这个装置测量土壤里的湿度。

examples.en: Silence was just a device to make us talk.
examples.cn: 沉默只是一种让我们开口的手段。

examples.en: The writer uses repetition as a poetic device.
examples.cn: 这位作家把重复当作一种诗歌手法。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 device 记成「地歪死」：de 是分开，vis 是看，把东西分开来看，看清结构再装成一件装置。

root: 来自古法语 devis（计划、划分），源头是拉丁语 dividere（分开），与动词 devise 同源后在英语中分化。本义是计划或设计，十六世纪起转指照设计造出的物件，再引申为手段与文学手法。

sensesIntro.en: From a plan drawn on paper, to the machine built from it, to a trick or a turn of style.
sensesIntro.cn: 从画在纸上的计划，到照它造出的机器，再到一个花招或一种笔法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small machine opened on a table, its parts laid bare.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台小机器在桌上被拆开，零件都露在外面。

branches.en: The first sense is the plan turned into hardware.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是计划变成了硬件。

branches.en: The second sense is a plan that needs no parts at all.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是根本不需要零件的计划。

branches.en: The third sense is a plan made of words.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是用词语做成的计划。

branches.en: A machine and a trick both exist to get a result.
branches.cn: 机器与花招，都是为得到一个结果而存在。

branches.en: A trick and a literary device both shape how you respond.
branches.cn: 花招与文学手法，都在塑造你的反应。

intro.en: Device belongs to a family about planning, dividing and building something useful.
intro.cn: device 属于一族词，围绕计划、划分与造出有用的东西。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base dividere means to divide, and the French plan word devis grew from it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 dividere 意为分开，法语里表示计划的 devis 就是从它长出来的。

items.meaning: a thing made from a plan
more than one piece of equipment
to invent a plan or method
items.exampleCN: 他们设计了一个简单的测试。
这个游戏设计得很巧妙。

items.example: Devising the rules took a week.
The deviser of the game is unknown.
items.exampleCN: 这个游戏的设计者不详。

items.example: He took a devious route home.
items.exampleCN: 他绕了一条弯路上回家。

definition_zh: 靴子；汽车后备箱；启动（计算机）
definition_en: a strong shoe that covers the ankle and part of the leg
core_image: 门口沾满泥的一双靴子
scene: 门口放着一双沾满泥的靴子。 A pair of muddy boots stood by the door.
sceneCN: 这里 boot 是「靴子」（第 1 个义项：包住脚踝和小腿的鞋）；句意是门口放着一双沾泥的靴子。

senses.title: A shoe that covers the ankle
senses.definition: a strong shoe covering the ankle and sometimes the leg
senses.definitionCN: 包住脚踝、有时包到小腿的结实鞋子
senses.example: A pair of muddy boots stood by the door.
senses.exampleCN: 门口放着一双沾泥的靴子。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, from a French word for a heavy shoe.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，来自法语中表示厚鞋的词。

senses.title: The luggage space of a car
senses.definition: the covered space at the back of a car for bags
senses.definitionCN: 汽车后部放行李的有盖空间
senses.example: Put the bags in the boot of the car.
senses.exampleCN: 把包放到汽车后备箱里。
senses.why: An old coach had a boot-shaped box for luggage at the back.
senses.whyCN: 旧式马车后部有个靴形的箱子放行李。

senses.title: To start a computer
senses.definition: to make a computer start working
senses.definitionCN: 让计算机开始运行
senses.example: The computer takes a minute to boot.
senses.exampleCN: 这台电脑启动需要一分钟。
senses.why: Starting a machine was compared to pulling yourself up by your bootstraps.
senses.whyCN: 启动机器被比作拉着自己的靴带站起来。

intro.en: Boot came from French, and its meaning spread from shoes to cars to computers.
intro.cn: boot 来自法语，意思从鞋子扩展到汽车，再到计算机。

items.en: bote meant a heavy shoe.
items.cn: bote 指厚重的鞋。

items.en: boot named leather footwear.
items.cn: boot 指皮革做的鞋靴。

items.en: boot named the luggage box on a coach.
items.cn: boot 指马车上的行李箱。

items.en: to boot became to start a computer.
items.cn: to boot 变成启动计算机。

items.en: boot covers footwear, car space and starting up.
items.cn: 如今 boot 兼指靴子、后备箱与启动。

note.en: The look-alike group differs by one letter; the near-meaning group names shoes and luggage spaces.
note.cn: 形近组只差一个字母；近义组是鞋与行李空间。

entries.definition: a small vehicle that travels on water
the part of a plant under the ground
a covering for the foot
the luggage space of a car

normalIntro.en: Boot is a shoe that protects the leg, and a box that protects the bags.
normalIntro.cn: boot 是护住小腿的鞋，也是护住行李的箱子。

normal.en: Boot and boots are singular and plural.
normal.cn: 单数是 boot，复数是 boots。

normal.en: Put your boots by the door.
normal.cn: 把靴子放在门边。

normal.en: Bags go in the boot of a car.
normal.cn: 行李放在汽车后备箱里。

normal.en: To boot a computer is to start it.
normal.cn: 启动电脑就是让它开始运行。

normal.en: Reboot means to start again.
normal.cn: reboot 意为重新启动。

abstract.en: See muddy boots on a doorstep.
abstract.cn: 想象门口台阶上沾泥的靴子。

abstract.en: See a suitcase packed into a car boot.
abstract.cn: 想象行李箱被塞进后备箱。

abstract.en: See a screen lighting up at startup.
abstract.cn: 想象开机时亮起的屏幕。

examples.en: A pair of muddy boots stood by the door.
examples.cn: 门口放着一双沾泥的靴子。

examples.en: Put the bags in the boot of the car.
examples.cn: 把包放到汽车后备箱里。

examples.en: The computer takes a minute to boot.
examples.cn: 这台电脑启动需要一分钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 boot 想成「不特」：靴子不特别好看但很耐穿，一脚踩下去连泥都不怕。

root: boot 源自法语 bote（厚鞋），十四世纪指皮革靴，十七世纪指马车上的行李箱，二十世纪又用来表示计算机启动。

sensesIntro.en: A strong shoe, a car's luggage space, and the act of starting a computer.
sensesIntro.cn: 结实的靴子、汽车放行李的空间，以及启动计算机。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of muddy boots by the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：门口一双沾泥的靴子。

branches.en: a pair of boots
branches.cn: 一双靴子

branches.en: a bootlace
branches.cn: 靴带

branches.en: the car boot
branches.cn: 汽车后备箱

branches.en: a full boot
branches.cn: 装满的后备箱

branches.en: boot the computer
branches.cn: 启动电脑

intro.en: Boot makes compounds and takes the prefix re-.
intro.cn: boot 可以构成复合词，也能加前缀 re-。

latinIntro.en: The base is Old French; the items below are related in meaning.
latinIntro.cn: 词基来自古法语，下面的词只在意思上相关。

definition_zh: 布丁；甜点心；（英式）餐后甜点；灌肠类咸食
definition_en: a cooked sweet dish made with milk, eggs, flour or rice; in British use, the sweet course after a meal; also a savoury mixture cooked in a skin or mould
core_image: 一只倒扣在盘上的焦糖布丁，勺子一碰就轻轻晃动
scene: 晚餐收桌之前，她从冰箱端出那只冷瓷碗，揭盖撒上一撮糖。 For dessert the children each had a bowl of steamed pudding.
sceneCN: 这里 pudding 是「餐后甜点」（第 2 个义项：正餐之后的甜点心）；句意为甜点时孩子们每人吃了一碗蒸布丁。画面里可留意：冷瓷碗、揭开的盖、糖罐。

pos.zh: 布丁；甜点；餐后甜点；咸味布丁

derivatives.zh: pudding 的口语缩略，指甜点
pudding 加 -y，指软得像布丁的
pudding 的复合词，指血肠，保留了古老的咸味义

senses.title: A soft sweet dish of milk, eggs or flour
senses.definition: a soft cooked dish made with milk, eggs, sugar, flour or rice, eaten cold or warm
senses.definitionCN: 用牛奶、蛋、糖、面粉或米做的软质熟食，冷热皆可食用
senses.example: The caramel pudding wobbled when the spoon touched it.
senses.exampleCN: 勺子一碰，焦糖布丁轻轻晃动。
senses.why: The word began as a sausage-like dish tied in a skin, and the soft, packed texture of those puddings carried over to the sweet mixtures cooked the same way.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指灌在肠衣里的紧实食物；那种软实、压紧的质地延续到同样烹制的甜 mixture 上，于是甜布丁继承了这个名字。

senses.title: The sweet course after a meal
senses.definition: in British English, the sweet dish served at the end of a meal, whatever it is made of
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中正餐结束时上的甜食，不论原料是什么
senses.example: There was fruit for pudding instead of cake.
senses.exampleCN: 甜点上是水果，而不是蛋糕。
senses.why: Once the sweet course of an English dinner was normally a pudding, the name of the dish extended to the whole course, the way dinner itself once named any meal.
senses.whyCN: 英式晚餐的甜点环节通常是某种布丁，于是菜名扩展成整个环节的名称，就像 dinner 一度泛指任何一餐。

senses.title: A savoury mixture cooked in a skin or mould
senses.definition: a savoury dish such as black pudding or Yorkshire pudding, cooked in a casing or a batter
senses.definitionCN: 血肠、约克郡布丁一类咸食，用肠衣灌制或用面糊烘烤
senses.example: Black pudding still keeps the word's oldest, savoury meaning.
senses.exampleCN: 血肠仍保留着这个词最古老的咸味含义。
senses.why: The earliest English puddings were sausages: meat and grain stuffed into a skin and boiled, and that savoury branch survives in a few fixed names.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的 pudding 就是香肠：肉与谷物灌进肠衣水煮；这一咸味支系如今只保存在少数固定名称里。

intro.en: Pudding goes back through Old French boudin, a sausage, to Latin botellus, a small sausage; English first used the word for savoury stuffed dishes, and only later for the sweet ones.
intro.cn: pudding 经古法语 boudin（香肠）上溯到拉丁语 botellus（小香肠）。英语最初用它指咸味的灌制食物，后来才转指甜点。

items.en: Botellus was a small sausage, a diminutive built on botulus, the word for a stuffed casing of meat.
items.cn: botellus 指小香肠，是 botulus（灌装的肉肠）的小词形式。

items.en: Old French boudin meant sausage and black pudding, and it kept the sausage idea as the word crossed into England.
items.cn: 古法语 boudin 指香肠与血肠，这个词进入英格兰时仍带着灌肠的观念。

items.en: Middle English puddynge named boiled savoury dishes in a skin, sweet or plain, all sharing the stuffed, packed texture.
items.cn: 中古英语 puddynge 指灌在肠衣里水煮的咸味或素净食物，共同点是紧实、填满的质地。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the sweet, flour-and-milk kinds grew dominant, and pudding settled as the name of the dessert course.
items.cn: 十七世纪起，面粉与牛奶做的甜布丁渐成主流，pudding 定格为餐后甜点的名称。

items.en: Modern English keeps both tracks: sweet puddings everywhere, and the old savoury sense in black pudding and Yorkshire pudding.
items.cn: 现代英语两条线并存：甜布丁处处可见，古老的咸味义则保存在 black pudding 与 Yorkshire pudding 里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words close in spelling or on the same sausage stem; the near-meaning group collects other words for sweet courses.
note.cn: 形近组收拼写相近或同属「香肠」词源的词；近义组收其他指餐后甜食的说法。

entries.definition: A small pool of water on the ground; only the spelling is close.
entries.definitionCN: 地上的小水洼；只是拼写相近，词义无关。

entries.definition: A French sausage, the direct relative of pudding in its oldest sense.
entries.definitionCN: 一种法式香肠，是 pudding 最古义的直系亲属。

entries.definition: A British blood sausage, keeping the savoury branch of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 英式血肠，保留了这个词的咸味分支。

entries.definition: The sweet course at the end of a meal; the American-default word.
entries.definitionCN: 正餐结束时的甜点环节；美式默认用词。

entries.definition: British informal for the dessert course.
entries.definitionCN: 英式口语中对甜点环节的说法。

entries.definition: A sweet sauce or set dish made of milk and eggs, often served with pudding.
entries.definitionCN: 用奶与蛋做的甜酱或凝冻，常与布丁同食。

normalIntro.en: The word is a sausage that turned sweet, so every hook follows that journey from casing to caramel.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一根变甜的香肠，所以每个记忆钩都跟着它从肠衣走向焦糖。

normal.en: Latin botellus is a small sausage; pudding began its English life as exactly that.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 botellus 是小香肠；pudding 在英语里的最初身份正是这个。

normal.en: Black pudding and Yorkshire pudding are the survivors of the savoury branch.
normal.cn: black pudding 与 Yorkshire pudding 是咸味分支的幸存者。

normal.en: In Britain, asking what is for pudding asks for the dessert course, not for one dish.
normal.cn: 在英国，问 what's for pudding 问的是甜点环节吃什么，而不是某道具体的菜。

normal.en: Steamed, boiled and baked puddings all keep the packed-in-a-mould idea.
normal.cn: 蒸、煮、烤的布丁都保留着「装进模子压实」的观念。

normal.en: Pud is the kitchen-short form, as natural as custard on the side.
normal.cn: pud 是厨房里的简称，就像旁边那勺 custard 一样自然。

abstract.en: A pudding is comfort with a skin on it: warmth packed into a shape.
abstract.cn: 布丁是裹着外皮的安慰：把温暖压实成一种形状。

abstract.en: Words drift from savoury to sweet as dinner tables do, and nobody votes on the change.
abstract.cn: 词义从咸转甜，正如餐桌口味迁移，没有人就此投票。

abstract.en: The same word can serve blood sausage and caramel custard, because texture outlives taste.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能指血肠又能指焦糖蛋奶冻，因为质地比味道活得更久。

examples.en: Grandmother's bread pudding used up every stale loaf.
examples.cn: 祖母的面包布丁把每块隔夜面包都用掉了。

examples.en: The Christmas pudding was set alight at the table.
examples.cn: 圣诞布丁在餐桌上被点了火。

examples.en: He had rice pudding for pudding, as he did every Sunday.
examples.cn: 他甜点吃米布丁，每个星期天都如此。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「扑定」——勺子一碰布丁，扑地晃了一下又定住，记住 pudding 是布丁。

root: 古法语 boudin（香肠、血肠）← 拉丁语 botellus（小香肠，botulus 的指小形式）；英语 pudding 最初指灌肠类咸食，十七世纪起转为甜点义，咸味支系保留在 black pudding 等固定名中。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a packed, cooked dish; the senses run from the soft sweet mixture, to the whole dessert course in British use, to the savoury sausage-dish where the word began.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「压紧烹熟的一道食物」；义项从软质甜 mixture，到英式的整个甜点环节，再回到这个词出发时的咸味灌肠。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a caramel pudding turned out onto a plate, wobbling under the first spoonful.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只倒扣在盘上的焦糖布丁，第一勺落下时轻轻晃动。

branches.en: a mould turned out, caramel running down the sides
branches.cn: 扣出模子、焦糖沿边流下的布丁

branches.en: the trolley wheeled in after the main course
branches.cn: 主菜之后推进来的甜点车

branches.en: a blood sausage sliced at breakfast
branches.cn: 早餐桌上切成片的血肠

branches.en: the same casing, once stuffed with meat and once with sugar
branches.cn: 同一种肠衣，一次灌肉，一次灌糖

branches.en: one word covering both ends of the meal
branches.cn: 一个词同时覆盖餐桌的两端

intro.en: The word rests on a Latin sausage word, its French descendant, the Middle English dish name, and the suffixes and compounds that grew around the dessert.
intro.cn: 这个词立足于拉丁语的「香肠」、其法语后裔、中古英语的菜名，以及围绕甜点长出的后缀与复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin botulus and its diminutive botellus are the recorded ancestors; anything earlier is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 有记录的祖先是拉丁语 botulus 及其指小形式 botellus；更早的来源不确定。

items.meaning: a sweet or savoury cooked dish
