items.meaningCN: 配烤肉的面糊烘烤食品

definition_zh: 最终；终于
definition_en: in the end, especially after a long time or many difficulties
core_image: 一条长长的路终于走到尽头，前方出现一扇门
scene: 经过多次失败，他终于找到了正确的方法。 After many failures, he eventually found the right method.
sceneCN: 这里 eventually 是「最终」（第 1 个义项：经历一段时间或困难之后终于如此）；句意：经过多次失败，他终于找到了正确的方法。

senses.title: In the end
senses.definition: at the end of a long process or period
senses.definitionCN: 在漫长过程或时期的末尾
senses.example: The train eventually arrived two hours late.
senses.exampleCN: 火车最终晚点两小时到达。
senses.why: The word comes from event, so it points to the outcome that finally comes.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自 event，因此指向最终到来的结果。

senses.title: As a final outcome
senses.definition: used to describe what happens as the final result
senses.definitionCN: 用于说明作为最终结果而发生的事
senses.example: The delay eventually cost them the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误最终让他们失去了合同。
senses.why: Eventual describes the last outcome, and the adverb points to that end point.
senses.whyCN: eventual 描述最后的结果，副词则指向那个终点。

intro.en: Eventually is eventual plus -ly, from Latin eventus, an outcome.
intro.cn: eventually 是 eventual 加 -ly，源自拉丁语 eventus（结果）。

items.en: Eventus means an outcome.
items.cn: eventus 意为结果。

items.en: Eventual means happening at the end.
items.cn: eventual 意为最终发生的。

items.en: The adverb eventually marks the end of a process.
items.cn: 副词 eventually 标记过程的终点。

items.en: It often suggests delay or difficulty.
items.cn: 它常暗示延误或困难。

items.en: Eventually is common in narrative and reports.
items.cn: eventually 常见于叙事与报告中。

note.en: Eventually is close to finally and in the end, with a sense of long delay.
note.cn: eventually 与 finally、in the end 相近，带有长期拖延的意味。

entries.definition: final
a happening
a possible outcome
after a long time
finally, after everything is considered
finally, when everything is over

normalIntro.en: Eventually marks the door at the end of a very long corridor.
normalIntro.cn: eventually 标记着漫长走廊尽头的那扇门。

normal.en: Eventually become means become so after time.
normal.cn: eventually become 意为经过时间之后成为。

normal.en: Eventually lead to means cause in the end.
normal.cn: eventually lead to 意为最终导致。

normal.en: Eventually agree means agree after long talks.
normal.cn: eventually agree 意为长时间商谈后同意。

normal.en: Sooner or later is a close everyday phrase.
normal.cn: sooner or later 是意思接近的日常短语。

normal.en: Compare finally: finally can mark the last item, eventually stresses the long wait.
normal.cn: 对比 finally：finally 可标记最后一项，eventually 强调漫长等待。

abstract.en: Picture a train that is late but still arrives.
abstract.cn: 想象一列晚点却终究到站的火车。

abstract.en: Imagine a seed that grows after a long winter.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子在漫长冬天后发芽。

abstract.en: Think of a page turned after many chapters.
abstract.cn: 想象翻过许多章节之后终于翻到的一页。

examples.en: She eventually agreed to help us.
examples.cn: 她最终同意帮助我们。

examples.en: The plan eventually failed.
examples.cn: 这个计划最终失败了。

examples.en: They eventually moved to a smaller house.
examples.cn: 他们最终搬进了一所较小的房子。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「event（事件）＋ ually」——所有事件走到最后，就是最终；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 eventus（结果）→ eventual（最终的）＋ -ly → eventually，核心义「经过漫长过程后到达结果」。

sensesIntro.en: Eventually first means in the end after a long time, and then describes the final outcome itself.
sensesIntro.cn: eventually 先指经过漫长时间后终于如此，再描述最终的结局本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door at the far end of a long corridor.
core.cn: 核心意象：漫长走廊尽头的一扇门。

branches.en: The main sense is reaching the end at last.
branches.cn: 主要义项是终于到达终点。

branches.en: The word can also label the final result.
branches.cn: 这个词也能标记最终结果。

branches.en: The long wait and the final outcome belong together.
branches.cn: 漫长等待与最终结果彼此相连。

branches.en: Delay is often implied but not required.
branches.cn: 延误常被暗示，但并非必需。

branches.en: Reports use the word to close a sequence.
branches.cn: 报告用这个词收束一系列事件。

intro.en: Eventually is eventual plus -ly, with event at the root.
intro.cn: eventually 是 eventual 加 -ly，词根是 event。

latinIntro.en: Latin eventus, an outcome, gives event and eventually.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 eventus（结果）衍生出 event 与 eventually。

definition_zh: 首领；酋长；主要的；首席的
definition_en: the leader of a group or an organization, or most important and highest in rank
core_image: 站在队伍最前面的那个人
scene: 会议桌两端坐满了人，屋里渐渐安静。 The chief of the village spoke last and everyone listened.
sceneCN: 这里 chief 指「首领」（第 1 个义项：群体或组织的领导者）；句意是村里的首领最后发言，所有人都在听。

senses.title: The leader of a group
senses.definition: the person who leads a group, a tribe or an organization
senses.definitionCN: 领导群体、部落或组织的人
senses.example: The village chief settled the dispute himself.
senses.exampleCN: 村长亲自解决了这场争端。
senses.why: The Latin word for head gave the name of the person at the head of a body of people.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表示「头」的词，给出了站在一群人最前面那个人的称呼。

senses.title: Most important
senses.definition: most important among several things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 同类事物中最重要的
senses.example: The chief reason for the delay was the weather.
senses.exampleCN: 延误的主要原因是天气。
senses.why: The head is the top of the body, so the adjective came to mean topmost in importance.
senses.whyCN: 头是身体的顶端，因此形容词表示重要性上位居最高。

senses.title: Highest in rank
senses.definition: holding the highest position in a profession or an office
senses.definitionCN: 在某行业或机构中居于最高职位的
senses.example: She was appointed chief engineer of the project.
senses.exampleCN: 她被任命为该项目的总工程师。
senses.why: Rank is pictured as height, so the head word marks the top post in a title.
senses.whyCN: 等级被想象成高低，因此这个「头」词标记出头衔中的最高职位。

intro.en: Chief is the Latin word for head, carried through French into English.
intro.cn: chief 是拉丁语中表示「头」的词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Caput meant the head of a person or an animal.
items.cn: 拉丁语 caput 指人或动物的头。

items.en: Chief meant the head, both of a body and of a group.
items.cn: 古法语 chief 既指身体的头，也指群体的头。

items.en: Chief named the leading person of a household or a band.
items.cn: 英语 chief 指家庭或队伍中的领头人。

items.en: The same form began to work as an adjective meaning principal.
items.cn: 同一形式开始作形容词，意为首要的。

items.en: Chief covers leaders, top posts and the most important reason.
items.cn: 如今 chief 涵盖首领、最高职位与最重要的理由。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the same long vowel or the same origin, while the meaning group names leaders.
note.cn: 形近组共享相同的长元音或同一来源，近义组列出领导者。

entries.definition: the head cook of a kitchen
a person who steals
a community ruled by a chief
a person who guides a group
the person in charge of a group
the most important of several things

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the head root caput, the chef doublet and the rank sense of chief.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子利用「头」词根 caput、同源词 chef 以及 chief 的职位义。

normal.en: Chief and chef are twins: the French form became the cook, the English one the leader.
normal.cn: chief 与 chef 是一对双胞胎：法语形式成了厨师，英语形式成了首领。

normal.en: Chief hides caput, the Latin head, also seen in capital and captain.
normal.cn: chief 里藏着拉丁语「头」caput，capital 与 captain 也含这个词根。

normal.en: A chief is at the head of people; a chief reason is at the head of a list.
normal.cn: chief 是人前的头，也是理由清单上的头。

normal.en: The plural chiefs simply adds an s after two consonants.
normal.cn: 复数 chiefs 只需在词尾加 s。

normal.en: Editor in chief puts the head word after the job, a common newspaper title.
normal.cn: editor in chief 把「头」词放在职务之后，是常见的报纸头衔。

abstract.en: Picture one figure standing a step ahead of a long line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人站在长队前面半步。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised to quiet a whole hall.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手举起，让整个大厅安静下来。

abstract.en: Picture a name plate reading chief engineer on a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上放着一块写着总工程师的名牌。

examples.en: The chief called the meeting to order.
examples.cn: 首领宣布会议开始。

examples.en: Safety is our chief concern.
examples.cn: 安全是我们最主要的关切。

examples.en: He was chief of the department for ten years.
examples.cn: 他担任该部门主管十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: chief 与 chef 同源，都是「头」：厨房的头是主厨，人群的头是首领。

root: 源自拉丁语 caput（头），经古法语 chief 进入英语，既作名词「首领」，也作形容词「首要的」。

sensesIntro.en: The head of a body of people gives the leader, and the head as the topmost part gives both the important and the highest-ranked senses.
sensesIntro.cn: 一群人中的「头」给出首领义，而作为最顶端的「头」给出「主要」与「最高职位」两个义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the head of a body, human or social.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个身体或一个群体的「头」。

branches.en: The leader sense names a person.
branches.cn: 首领义项指一个人。

branches.en: The important sense ranks reasons and aims.
branches.cn: 主要义项给理由与目标排序。

branches.en: The rank sense builds titles such as chief engineer.
branches.cn: 职位义项构成总工程师这类头衔。

branches.en: A chief holds the chief post.
branches.cn: 首领占据最高的职位。

branches.en: Both adjective senses place something at the top.
branches.cn: 两个形容词义项都把某物置于顶端。

intro.en: Chief builds a small family from the Latin head root caput.
intro.cn: chief 从拉丁语「头」词根 caput 出发，构成一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput, the head, also gives capital, captain and the French chef.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 caput（头）也给出 capital、captain 以及法语的 chef。

items.example: The land is chiefly used for grazing.
items.exampleCN: 这片土地主要用来放牧。

items.example: The chieftain wore a heavy cloak.

items.meaning: a society led by a chief
the leader of a team or a ship

items.exampleCN: caput 是 chief 背后的词。

definition_zh: 适应；使适应；改编；改装；改造
definition_en: to change your behaviour or to change something else so that it fits new conditions, a new purpose, or a different audience
core_image: 一件原本合身的外套被改了几针，穿到另一个身形上又合身了
scene: 外婆搬进城里的小公寓，阳台朝北，她把旧藤椅挪了三次才坐得舒服。 She soon adapted to life in the small apartment.
sceneCN: 这里 adapt 是「适应新的生活条件」（第 1 个义项：人为适应新环境而改变自己的做法）；句意为她很快就适应了小公寓里的生活。

pos.zh: 动词：适应；使适应；改编；改装；改造
及物动词：改编（作品）；改装（物件）；调整（做法）以适合
不及物动词：适应（常与 to 连用）

collocations.phrase: adapt a novel for the screen
collocations.zh: 把小说改编成影视作品

collocations.phrase: adapt a building for wheelchair users
collocations.zh: 改造建筑以便轮椅使用者出入

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「适应；改编；改编作品」
由本词加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「能适应的；可改装的」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ive 构成，义为「适应性的；有适应能力的」
由本词加表示施动者或器具的后缀 -er 构成，义为「适配器；改编者」
adapter 的另一种拼写，多做英式拼法，指「适配器；转接头」

senses.title: Of a person: to fit into new conditions
senses.definition: to change your habits, behaviour or way of living so that you can live or work well in new conditions
senses.definitionCN: 改变习惯、做法或生活方式，以便在新的条件下顺利生活或工作
senses.example: It took her a month to adapt to the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了一个月才适应夜班。
senses.why: The Latin root aptus means fit; ad- adds toward, so the verb is literally to make oneself fitting for a situation.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 aptus 意为「合适」，前缀 ad- 表示「朝向」，所以这个动词本义就是「把自己调整到与情境相合」。

senses.title: Of a species: to become suited to its habitat
senses.definition: of a plant or animal, to develop features over generations that make survival in a particular environment more likely
senses.definitionCN: 指动植物经过许多代发展出某些特征，使其更容易在特定环境中存活
senses.example: These birds adapted to the colder coast within a few generations.
senses.exampleCN: 这些鸟在几代之内就适应了更寒冷的海岸。
senses.why: The same idea of fitting is stretched over time: what is fitted is not one body but a whole population and its surroundings.
senses.whyCN: 「合适」这层意思被拉长到时间尺度上：被调整到相合的不再是一个身体，而是整个种群与它的环境。

senses.title: Of the eyes: to adjust to light or dark
senses.definition: of the eyes or another sense organ, to become able to see or feel clearly after a change of light or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指眼睛等感觉器官在光线或环境改变后逐渐恢复清晰的感知
senses.example: Wait a moment while your eyes adapt to the darkness.
senses.exampleCN: 稍等一下，让眼睛适应黑暗。
senses.why: The fitting here happens inside the body and takes only seconds: the eye tunes itself until the image is clear again.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「相合」发生在身体内部，只消几秒：眼睛自行调整到图像重新清晰为止。

senses.title: To alter an object for a new use
senses.definition: to change the design or parts of an object so that it can be used for a different purpose
senses.definitionCN: 改变物体的设计或部件，使其能用于另一种用途
senses.example: He adapted an old coffee tin into a lamp holder.
senses.exampleCN: 他把一个旧咖啡罐改装成了灯座。
senses.why: If a thing must fit a new job, it is altered until it does; the object, not the person, is the one that changes.
senses.whyCN: 如果一件东西要胜任新用途，就把它改到合适为止；这里改变的是物，而不是人。

senses.title: To rewrite a story for screen or stage
senses.definition: to turn a book, play or other written work into a film, television series or stage production
senses.definitionCN: 把书、戏剧或其他文字作品改成电影、电视剧或舞台作品
senses.example: The studio adapted the novel into a six-part series.
senses.exampleCN: 制片方把那部小说改编成了六集剧集。
senses.why: A story written for one medium must be cut and reshaped until it fits another; the fit is between forms, not bodies.
senses.whyCN: 为一个媒介写的故事要经过删改与重塑，才能与另一个媒介相合；这里的「合身」发生在两种形式之间，与身体无关。

senses.title: To adjust lessons to a group of learners
senses.titleCN: 调整（教材、课程）以适合学习者
senses.definition: to change teaching materials, tasks or courses so that they suit the level and needs of a particular class
senses.definitionCN: 修改教材、任务或课程，使其适合某个班级的水平与需要
senses.example: Good teachers adapt the same worksheet for weaker classes.
senses.exampleCN: 好老师会把同一份练习改编给基础较弱的班级。
senses.why: The material is not wrong; it simply has to be fitted to the people using it, the same way clothes are taken in or let out.
senses.whyCN: 材料本身没有错，只是要量着使用者的身量改一改，就像衣服改肥改瘦。

senses.title: To modify a building or vehicle for disabled users
senses.titleCN: 改造（建筑、车辆）以便无障碍使用
senses.definition: to change a building, vehicle or piece of equipment so that people with disabilities can use it
senses.definitionCN: 改造建筑、车辆或设备，使残障人士也能使用
senses.example: The museum adapted its main entrance for wheelchair users.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆改造了正门，方便轮椅使用者出入。
senses.why: Here the fitting has a fixed shape in mind: the design is bent until a specific body can get through.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「相合」有一个明确的身体作参照：把设计改到某类身体也能通过为止。

senses.title: To change your manner to suit other people
senses.titleCN: 调整言谈举止以适合场合或对象
senses.definition: to change the way you speak or behave so that it suits a particular person, group or social occasion
senses.definitionCN: 改变说话或行事的方式，使之适合特定的人、群体或社交场合
senses.example: A good host adapts his tone to the guests at the table.
senses.exampleCN: 好的主人会按同桌客人的不同来调整自己的语气。
senses.why: What is fitted now is the self: the manner is adjusted the way a garment is, until it sits well in the room.
senses.whyCN: 这时被调整的就是自己：言谈像衣服一样被改到在场合里看着得体。

intro.en: Adapt is a Latin verb built from ad- and aptare, and English took it over in the sixteenth century with the idea of fitting already inside it.
intro.cn: adapt 是由拉丁语前缀 ad- 与动词 aptare 构成的，英语在十六世纪借入时，「使相合」的意思已经包含在里面。

items.en: Aptus meant 'fitted, suitable, apt'. It is generally connected with the verb apere, 'to fasten, attach', but the deeper origin of the root is uncertain.
items.cn: aptus 意为「合适的、恰当的」，一般认为与动词 apere「系上、连接」有关，但这个词根更早的来源不确定。

items.en: From aptus came the verb aptare, 'to fit, fasten, adjust', used of clothes, armour and equipment as well as of abstract matters.
items.cn: 由 aptus 生出动词 aptare，意为「使合适、系紧、调整」，既用于衣物、盔甲与装备，也用于抽象事物。

items.en: The prefix ad-, 'to, toward', plus aptare produced adaptare, 'to fit to, make suitable for'.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 表示「朝向」，与 aptare 合成 adaptare，意为「使合于、使适合于」。

items.en: English borrowed the word as adapt, first in the sense 'to fit or suit', and the spelling has been stable since then.
items.cn: 英语借入后写作 adapt，最初义为「使相合、使适合」，此后拼写基本未变。

items.en: The biological sense 'to become suited to a habitat' spread in the nineteenth century, and the film and stage sense of adapting a work in the twentieth.
items.cn: 「适应栖息环境」的生物学义在十九世纪流行开来，「改编作品」的影视与舞台义则在二十世纪扩展。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the family built on aptus plus one accidental twin; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of adjusting, modifying and tailoring.
note.cn: 形近组收以 aptus 为根的一族词，外加一个纯属拼写相近的词；近义组收调整、修改与量体裁衣一类的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of fitting something to new conditions, or for a work rewritten for another medium.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适应、改编、改编作品」，指使某物合于新条件的行为，或为另一媒介改写的作品。

entries.definition: Able to change easily in order to suit new conditions; formed with the suffix -able.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「能适应的、可改装的」，由本词加后缀 -able 构成。

entries.definition: A device that lets one plug or part fit another, or a person who rewrites a work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适配器、转接头」，也指改编者；由本词加后缀 -er 构成。

entries.definition: Very skilled at something; it looks close to adapt but comes from Latin adeptus, a person who has attained something.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「熟练的、内行的」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，它出自拉丁语 adeptus「已达到者」。

entries.definition: To change something slightly, often a machine or a position, so that it works or looks right.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「调整、校准」，多指小幅改动机器或位置，使之正常或合适。

entries.definition: To change something in part, usually to improve it; more deliberate and formal than adapt.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「修改、改进」，通常指部分改动，比 adapt 更有计划性、语气更正式。

entries.definition: To change your plans or arrangements so that someone's needs are met.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「迁就、顾及」，指改变安排以满足某人的需要。

entries.definition: To make or change something for a particular person or purpose, as a tailor cuts cloth.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「量身定制、按需调整」，像裁缝裁布一样为特定的人或目的改动。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin base aptus and the three patterns the verb actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用真实的拉丁词基 aptus，以及这个动词实际出现的三种结构。

normal.en: Aptus is Latin for fitted, so adapt is what you do until something is fitted to its situation.
normal.cn: aptus 在拉丁语里就是「合适的」，adapt 就是一直改到某物与情境相合。

normal.en: The prefix ad- means toward, so the fitting is always pointed at someone or something.
normal.cn: 前缀 ad- 表示「朝向」，所以这种「合适」总是朝着某人或某物而去。

normal.en: Adapt to a place, adapt something for a person, and adapt a book from a novel are the three common patterns.
normal.cn: 接 to 说环境，接 for 说对象，接 from 说来源，是三种常见结构。

normal.en: Adaptation, adaptable and adapter all keep the same Latin base.
normal.cn: adaptation、adaptable、adapter 都保留同一个拉丁词基。

normal.en: In biology a species adapts; in film a studio adapts a novel; both fit one thing to another.
normal.cn: 生物学里物种 adapt，电影圈里制片方 adapt 一部小说，两者都是把一个东西改到与另一个相合。

abstract.en: Picture a jacket taken in at the waist: the person has not changed, the jacket has.
abstract.cn: 想象一件外套在腰间被收了几针：人没变，变的是外套。

abstract.en: Fit is a relation, not a quality: the same key opens one door and fails at the next.
abstract.cn: 「合」是一种关系，不是一种属性：同一把钥匙开得了这扇门，却开不了下一扇。

abstract.en: Every new place asks the same question: what here must be altered, the world or me?
abstract.cn: 每到一个新地方都在问同一个问题：要改的是这里的东西，还是我自己？

examples.en: My parents adapted quickly to video calls.
examples.cn: 我爸妈很快就适应了视频通话。

examples.en: The director adapted the book for a younger audience.
examples.cn: 导演把这本书改编成了适合年轻观众看的版本。

examples.en: We adapted the spare room into a small office.
examples.cn: 我们把那间空房改成了小办公室。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「鹅大夫特」——鹅大夫特别会随环境换法子，旧衣改一改就合身：适应、改装。

root: 拉丁语 aptus「合适的」加前缀 ad-「朝向」，先有 aptare「使合适」，再合成 adaptare「使合于」。aptus 一般认为与 apere「系上、连接」有关，更早来源不确定；英语于十六世纪借入。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses apply one adjustment to a different thing: a person, a species, the eyes, an object, a story, a lesson, a building, or a manner of speech.

branches.en: THE PERSON: habits are altered until daily life in a new place runs smoothly.

branches.en: THE BODY: a population changes over generations, and the eye changes in seconds.

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a tin, a car or a doorway is rebuilt until a new use fits it.
branches.cn: 物件线：罐子、车辆或门口被改造到能容纳新用途。

branches.en: THE TEXT: a story or a worksheet is reshaped until another audience can take it in.

branches.en: THE SELF: the last thing fitted is your own tone of voice.

normal.en: A polite no is also a way of stepping aside.
normal.cn: 礼貌的拒绝，也是一种让开。

normal.en: Towns decline one closed shop at a time.
normal.cn: 小镇是一间店一间店地衰落的。

normal.en: The same bending away that refuses an offer also lowers a number.
normal.cn: 把提议绕开的那一弯，也把数字压了下去。

normal.en: Grammar declines nouns the way a road declines a hill.
normal.cn: 语法让名词变格，就像道路顺坡而下。

abstract.en: Picture a pencil line easing down a page.
abstract.cn: 想象铅笔线在纸上缓缓下滑。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised to say no thanks.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手抬起来表示谢绝。

abstract.en: Picture a shop window with paper over the glass.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇玻璃上糊了纸的店窗。

examples.en: Sales declined sharply after the summer.
examples.cn: 夏天过后销量急剧下滑。

examples.en: She declined the invitation with a short note.
examples.cn: 她写了一封短笺婉拒了邀请。

examples.en: The industry is in decline and few young people join it.
examples.cn: 这个行业正在衰退，很少有年轻人入行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 decline 记成「低可赖」：de 是低，cline 像「靠」，坡一低，人就只能靠着往下溜。

root: 源自拉丁语 declinare（弯开、偏斜），词根 clinare 意为弯曲。它的两个主要意思都从「弯」来：数字往下弯是下降，人往旁边弯是婉拒；语法上的变格用法也沿用同一个比喻。

sensesIntro.en: From a line bending downward, to an offer bent aside, to a long state of weakening.
sensesIntro.cn: 从向下弯的线，到被让开的提议，再到长期变弱的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line easing gently downward across a page.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条线在纸页上缓缓向下。

branches.en: The first sense is quantity dropping on a chart.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是图表上的数量往下掉。

branches.en: The second sense is a person stepping politely aside.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是一个人礼貌地让到一边。

branches.en: The third sense is a long slope that no single fall explains.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是一道慢坡，单次下跌解释不了。

branches.en: A small fall repeated becomes a long decline.
branches.cn: 一次小跌反复发生，就成了长期衰退。

branches.en: To decline an offer is to let it fall away from you.
branches.cn: 婉拒一个提议，就是让它从身边落下去。

intro.en: Decline holds the -clin- stem, shared with incline, recline and declination.
intro.cn: decline 带着 -clin- 词干，与 incline、recline、declination 同族。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is clinare, to bend; Greek had a related word for a bed, kline.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 clinare（弯曲），希腊语里表示床的 kline 与之同源。

items.example: The declining birth rate worried them.
items.exampleCN: 下降的出生率让他们担心。
拉丁语变格遵循清楚的规律。
这个名词没有词形变化。

items.meaning: to turn an offer down politely
items.example: He declined the offer with thanks.
The chart shows a sharp decline.
Demand for coal is on the decline.

latinEntries.example: Clinare gives English decline and incline.
latinEntries.exampleCN: clinare 给英语带来 decline 和 incline。

definition_zh: 获得；获取；习得；收购；染上
definition_en: to get or gain something, especially by effort, purchase or experience
core_image: 伸手去够，够了几次，终于把想要的东西拿到自己这边
scene: 她在国外住了两年，回来时已经能说一口当地话。 Children acquire language faster than adults.
sceneCN: 这里 acquire 指在生活环境中自然学会一门语言（第 2 个义项：通过练习习得技能或语言）；句意为孩子习得语言比成年人快。

pos.zh: 动词：获得；获取；习得；收购；染上

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -sition 构成，义为「获取；收购；习得」
由本词加 -itive 构成，义为「贪求的；渴望占有的」
由本词加 -er 构成，义为「获得者；收购方」
由本词加 -able 构成，义为「可获得的；可学会的」

senses.title: Obtain something by effort or payment
senses.definition: to get something, especially by working for it or by paying for it
senses.definitionCN: 得到某物，尤指通过努力或付钱取得
senses.example: They saved for years to acquire the small flat.
senses.exampleCN: 他们攒了好几年钱才买下那套小公寓。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to seek, and the prefix added 'in addition'; what you have sought and gained comes to rest on your side.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词本义是「寻求」，前缀又加上「额外、到手」的意思；寻求并且得手的东西，就停到了你这一边。

senses.title: Gain a skill or language through practice
senses.definition: to learn a skill, habit or language gradually, especially by using it
senses.definitionCN: 逐步学会某种技能、习惯或语言，尤指在使用中学会
senses.example: Children acquire language faster than adults.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子习得语言比成年人快。
senses.why: A skill is not handed over; it is sought again and again until it stays with you, so the seeking verb covers learning.
senses.whyCN: 技能不是别人递过来的，而是一次次去够，直到它留在你身上；于是「寻求」这个动词也覆盖了「学会」。

senses.title: Buy or take over a company
senses.definition: to buy a company or a large share of it, or to gain control of it
senses.definitionCN: 买下一家公司或其很大一部分股份，或取得其控制权
senses.example: The chain acquired three smaller rivals last year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家连锁企业去年收购了三家较小的对手。
senses.why: A company is simply a very large object of purchase, and the old verb of getting takes on the cool tone of business.
senses.whyCN: 一家公司无非是一件非常大的可购之物，「取得」这个老动词于是带上了商业的冷静口气。

senses.title: Come to like something gradually
senses.definition: to develop a liking for something, especially in the phrase acquire a taste for
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐对某物产生喜爱，尤用于短语 acquire a taste for
senses.example: He acquired a taste for black coffee during his years abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 在国外那几年，他慢慢喜欢上了黑咖啡。
senses.why: Liking, too, can be something you come to possess: it arrives by repeated exposure, like an object slowly carried home.
senses.whyCN: 喜好也可以是一件「得到」的东西：它靠反复接触慢慢到来，像一件被一点点搬回家的物件。

senses.title: Gain knowledge or information
senses.definition: to get knowledge, information or data, often by searching or collecting it
senses.definitionCN: 获得知识、信息或数据，常通过查找与收集
senses.example: The team acquired enough data to test the theory.
senses.exampleCN: 团队获取了足够的数据来检验这个理论。
senses.why: Information is what you go out and seek; the word keeps the original hunt inside the modern lab.
senses.whyCN: 信息正是你出去寻找的东西；这个词把原始的「搜寻」保留在现代实验室里。

senses.title: Come to have a reputation or quality
senses.definition: to develop a reputation, label or quality over time, often without intending to
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间形成某种名声、标签或特征，常非有意为之
senses.example: The street acquired a reputation for cheap food and loud music.
senses.exampleCN: 这条街渐渐有了「吃食便宜、音乐吵闹」的名声。
senses.why: A reputation is not bought; it accumulates around a person or place until it belongs to them, and the word treats it as a possession.
senses.whyCN: 名声不是买来的，它围绕一个人或一个地方累积，直到归其所有；这个词便把它当成一份所有物。

senses.title: Catch a disease or condition
senses.definition: to become infected with a disease, or to develop a condition such as immunity
senses.definitionCN: 感染某种疾病，或形成免疫力之类的状态
senses.example: Patients can acquire the infection during a long hospital stay.
senses.exampleCN: 病人可能在长期住院期间染上这种感染。
senses.why: Illness is something that comes to settle in the body without being invited, so even a thing you do not want is 'acquired'.
senses.whyCN: 疾病是不请自来、在身体里住下的东西，所以连你不想要的东西也会被说成「获得」。

senses.title: Gained after birth, not inherited
senses.definition: of a quality or condition, developed during life rather than present from birth
senses.definitionCN: 指某种品质或状况在生命过程中形成，而非与生俱来
senses.example: The doctor explained the difference between inherited and acquired traits.
senses.exampleCN: 医生解释了遗传特征与后天特征的区别。
senses.why: Science needed a word for what is added to an organism after it starts, and the old verb of getting supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要一个词来指「生命开始之后才添上去」的东西，而那个表示「取得」的老动词正好提供了它。

intro.en: Acquire is a Latin verb of seeking, with a prefix that means 'to' or 'in addition', carried into English through Old French.
intro.cn: acquire 是一个表示「寻求」的拉丁语动词，带一个意为「朝向、额外」的前缀，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: Quaerere meant 'to seek, search for, ask'; the same verb lies behind inquire, require, question and query.
items.cn: quaerere 意为「寻求、搜寻、询问」；inquire、require、question 与 query 都出自同一个动词。

items.en: The prefix ad- meant 'to, towards'. Before q it was written ac-, so ad plus quaerere appears as acquirere.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 意为「向、朝」。在 q 之前写作 ac-，因此 ad 加 quaerere 写作 acquirere。

items.en: Acquirere meant 'to get in addition, procure, gain'; its past participle acquisitus is the base of acquisition.
items.cn: acquirere 意为「额外获得、取得、得到」；其过去分词 acquisitus 是 acquisition 的基础。

items.en: Old French aquerre carried the verb towards English, and Middle English borrowed it in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 aquerre 把这个动词带向英语，中古英语在十五世纪借入。

items.en: The verb is recorded from the fifteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain, and the business sense 'buy a company' belongs to the twentieth century.
items.cn: 这个动词自十五世纪有记录；确切首见年代不确定，而「收购公司」的商业义属于二十世纪。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same Latin verb of seeking; the near-meaning group lists other ways of getting something.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁语「寻求」动词构成的一族词；近义组列出其他表示「得到」的说法。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of getting something, especially a company or a skill.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「获取、收购、习得」，尤指公司或技能。

entries.definition: To need something or demand it as necessary; the same Latin verb with re-.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「需要、要求」，是同一拉丁动词加 re- 构成。

entries.definition: To ask for information; literally to seek into something.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「询问、打听」，字面意思是「往里寻求」。

entries.definition: To declare someone not guilty; it only looks similar and comes from another Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「宣判无罪」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，来自另一个拉丁动词。

entries.definition: To get something, especially by effort; more formal than acquire and common with permissions.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「获得」，比 acquire 更正式，常与许可、批准搭配。

entries.definition: To get something useful or valuable over time, such as experience or weight.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「赢得、增加」，多指随着时间得到有用的东西，如经验或体重。

entries.definition: To obtain something with effort, often through a supplier or a formal process.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「设法取得」，常通过供应商或正式程序，语气正式。

entries.definition: To get money or respect in return for work or good conduct.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「挣得、赢得」，强调以工作或品行换取。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin verb of seeking and the phrases acquire appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面的钩子使用真实的拉丁语「寻求」动词，以及 acquire 常出现的搭配。

normal.en: Quaerere means to seek: acquire is what happens when the seeking ends in your hands.
normal.cn: quaerere 意为「寻求」：acquire 就是寻求结束时东西落在你手里。

normal.en: Inquire, require and acquire all hide the same quaerere.
normal.cn: inquire、require、acquire 都藏着同一个 quaerere。

normal.en: Acquire a taste for means the liking itself was slowly obtained.
normal.cn: acquire a taste for 意为连这份喜好也是慢慢得到的。

normal.en: An acquired taste is one you had to work towards.
normal.cn: an acquired taste 是需要你慢慢培养才喜欢的味道。

normal.en: In business, to acquire is simply to buy a whole company.
normal.cn: 在商业里，to acquire 就是买下一整家公司。

abstract.en: Picture a hand reaching for a fruit just out of range, then closing on it: that closing is the word.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸向差一点就够到的果子，然后握住：那一握就是这个词。

abstract.en: Skills, habits, reputations and even illnesses all arrive by the same route: something outside slowly becomes yours.
abstract.cn: 技能、习惯、名声，甚至疾病，都走同一条路：外面的东西慢慢变成你的。

abstract.en: The word is neutral about wanting: you can acquire a fortune or a cold.
abstract.cn: 这个词对「想不想要」保持中立：你可以 acquire 一笔财富，也可以 acquire 一场感冒。

examples.en: Children acquire language faster than adults.
examples.cn: 孩子习得语言比成年人快。

examples.en: They saved for years to acquire the small flat.
examples.cn: 他们攒了好几年钱才买下那套小公寓。

examples.en: He acquired a taste for black coffee during his years abroad.
examples.cn: 在国外那几年，他慢慢喜欢上了黑咖啡。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额快儿」——快点伸手去够，够到手就是获得、拿到。

root: 拉丁语 acquirere「额外取得、获得」由 ad-「向」加 quaerere「寻求」构成，ad- 在 q 前写作 ac-；过去分词 acquisitus 生出 acquisition。quaerere 同时也是 inquire、require、question 的词根。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense of acquire is the same movement: something outside is sought, reached and then belongs to you. The difference is what is being got, and whether you wanted it.
sensesIntro.cn: acquire 的每个义项都是同一个动作：外面的东西被寻求、被够到，然后归你所有。区别只在于得到的是什么，以及那是不是你想要的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand reaching out and closing on something it has been seeking.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手伸出去，把一直在找的东西握住。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: from a small purchase to a whole company, the word covers what can be got.
branches.cn: 物件线：从小件购买到整家公司，这个词覆盖一切能取得的东西。

branches.en: THE MIND: skills, languages and information are got by seeking them repeatedly.
branches.cn: 心智线：技能、语言与信息，都靠反复寻求才到手。

branches.en: THE APPETITE: even a liking can be slowly obtained, as in acquire a taste for.
branches.cn: 口味线：连喜好也能慢慢获得，如 acquire a taste for。

branches.en: THE UNINVITED: reputation and disease settle on a person without being asked for.
branches.cn: 不请自来线：名声与疾病未经邀请就落在一个人身上。

branches.en: THE TIMING: whatever is added after birth rather than inherited is marked as acquired.
branches.cn: 时间线：凡是出生之后才添上、而非遗传而来的，都标为后天的。

intro.en: Acquire is a Latin prefix plus a Latin verb of seeking, and English builds its family with ordinary endings.
intro.cn: acquire 是一个拉丁语前缀加一个表示「寻求」的拉丁语动词，英语用普通词尾扩展出词族。

latinIntro.en: Quaerere, acquirere and their forms are recorded Latin; only the deeper Indo-European root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: quaerere、acquirere 及其形式都是有记录的拉丁语，只有更早的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.example: It points the seeking towards an object.
items.exampleCN: 它把「寻求」指向某个对象。

items.meaningCN: ad- 在 q 前的同化形式
items.example: It appears in acquirere and in acquire.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在 acquirere 与 acquire 里。

items.example: Quaerere is the heart of the word.
Acquirere is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: acquirere 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: They acquired the land in stages.
items.exampleCN: 他们分阶段取得了这块地。

definition_zh: 原则；原理；准则；道义；（机器的）工作原理；本源（古义）
definition_en: a basic truth, rule, or belief that explains or guides how something works or how one should act
core_image: 一座建筑的承重柱：看不见整体，却撑着上面所有楼层
scene: 工程师向客户解释这台发动机。 Fuel burns, the piston moves, and the crank turns: the same principle drives every model in the catalogue.
sceneCN: 这里 principle 是「原理」（第 3、4 个义项：解释事物如何运作的基本道理；系统工作原理）；句意：燃料燃烧、活塞运动、曲轴转动，同一个原理驱动目录里的每一种型号。图中可辨识物件：发动机剖面、活塞、曲轴、燃烧室、示意图；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 原则；原理；准则；道义；本源（古义）

senses.title: A fundamental truth or rule
senses.definition: a basic rule or truth that other rules depend on
senses.definitionCN: 其他规则所依赖的基本规则或真理
senses.example: The course teaches the principles of economics.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课讲授经济学原理。
senses.why: Latin principium means 'a beginning, a first part'. A principle is where a subject starts: the first thing you must accept before the rest can be built.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 principium 意为“开端、第一部分”。principle 是一门学科的起点：在其余部分建立之前，你必须先接受的那第一件事。

senses.title: A moral rule of conduct
senses.definition: a belief about right behavior that guides a person
senses.definitionCN: 指导人行为的关于正当行为的信念
senses.example: She refused on principle to lie.
senses.exampleCN: 她出于原则拒绝撒谎。
senses.why: Morality turns the architectural image into a personal one: a principle is a load-bearing belief. Break it and the rest of the person's conduct must be rebuilt.
senses.whyCN: 道德把建筑意象变成个人意象：principle 是一根承重的信念。折断它，这个人其余的行为都得重建。

senses.title: A scientific law or mechanism
senses.definition: the basic way a natural process or device works
senses.definitionCN: 自然过程或装置运作的基本方式
senses.example: The principle behind the engine is simple.
senses.exampleCN: 这台发动机背后的原理很简单。
senses.why: Science uses the word for the explanatory core: not a specific result but the rule that generates results. The principle is what remains true across cases.
senses.whyCN: 科学用这个词指解释的核心：不是某个具体结果，而是产生结果的规则。原理是在各种情形中都成立的东西。

senses.title: The working rule of a system
senses.definition: the rule by which a machine, method, or organization operates
senses.definitionCN: 机器、方法或组织运作所依的规则
senses.example: The pump works on the principle of expanding air.
senses.exampleCN: 这个泵依空气膨胀的原理工作。
senses.why: Engineering names the operating rule of an artifact. The principle explains why the design works, which is why it can be transferred to new machines.
senses.whyCN: 工程学给人工物的运作规则命名。原理解释设计为何有效，因此可以迁移到新机器上。

senses.title: A personal code of conduct
senses.definition: a set of values a person has decided to live by
senses.definitionCN: 一个人决定遵行的价值体系
senses.example: He is a man of principle.
senses.exampleCN: 他是一个有原则的人。
senses.why: When a person owns principles, the word becomes a character description. To have principles is to have a structure that does not bend with convenience.
senses.whyCN: 当一个人拥有 principles，这个词就成了一种品格描述。有原则，就是有一套不随便利弯曲的结构。

senses.title: Origin or source (archaic)
senses.definition: in older usage, the beginning or source from which something comes
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法：事物由来的开端或源头
senses.example: Water was once held to be the principle of all things.
senses.exampleCN: 水曾被当作万物的本源。
senses.why: The oldest sense is 'beginning'. Greek philosophy asked for the arche, the first principle of things, and English used principle for that source before it narrowed to rules.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是“开端”。希腊哲学追问万物的 arche（第一原理），英语在收窄为“规则”之前，曾用 principle 指那个源头。

senses.title: In principle: as a theory
senses.definition: in the phrase in principle, as far as the basic idea is concerned
senses.definitionCN: 用于 in principle，就基本理念而言
senses.example: In principle the plan is sound.
senses.exampleCN: 原则上这个计划是合理的。
senses.why: The phrase separates theory from practice: the principle may hold even if the execution fails. It is a way of granting the idea without promising the result.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把理论与实行分开：即使执行失败，原理仍可成立。它是一种承认想法、却不承诺结果的说法。

senses.title: On principle: from conviction
senses.definition: in the phrase on principle, because of a moral or personal rule
senses.definitionCN: 用于 on principle，出于道德或个人规则
senses.example: He opposed the deal on principle.
senses.exampleCN: 他出于原则反对这笔交易。
senses.why: On principle marks a decision that is not pragmatic. The person is not weighing outcomes but obeying a rule, which is exactly what a principle is for.
senses.whyCN: on principle 标记一个非务实的选择。人不是在权衡结果，而是在服从规则——这正是原则的用途。

senses.title: A constituent element (archaic science)
senses.definition: in old chemistry and philosophy, a basic substance from which things are made
senses.definitionCN: 旧化学与哲学中构成事物的基本物质
senses.example: The four principles of the old chemistry were earth, water, air, and fire.
senses.exampleCN: 旧化学的四种要素是土、水、气、火。
senses.why: Before modern chemistry, 'principles' were the simple bodies into which matter could be resolved. The word then meant both beginning and ingredient.
senses.whyCN: 在现代化学之前，principles 是物质可被分解成的基本体。那时这个词兼指“开端”与“成分”。

intro.en: Principle comes from Latin principium, 'a beginning'. Its root princeps means 'first man', from primus 'first' plus capere 'to take'. The same root gives prince and principal, which is why principle and principal are so often confused.
intro.cn: principle 来自拉丁语 principium“开端”。其词根 princeps 意为“第一人”，由 primus“第一”加 capere“取”构成。同一个词根生成 prince 与 principal，所以 principle 与 principal 常被混淆。

items.en: First recorded as 'origin, source, fundamental truth', from Latin principium through Old French principe.
items.cn: 最早记录为“起源、源头、根本真理”，经古法语 principe 来自拉丁语 principium。

items.en: principium 'beginning, first part' comes from princeps 'first, chief', literally 'one who takes first place'.
items.cn: principium“开端、第一部分”来自 princeps“第一的、首要的”，字面为“占据第一位者”。

items.en: princeps = primus 'first' + capere 'to take, seize'. The chief is the one who takes the first place or the first share.
items.cn: princeps = primus“第一”+ capere“取、抓”。首领就是占据第一位或第一份的人。

items.en: principle comes from principium (a beginning, a rule); principal comes from principalis (first in rank). They share princeps but differ in meaning: a principle is a rule, a principal is a chief or a sum of money.
items.cn: principle 来自 principium（开端、规则）；principal 来自 principalis（等级第一）。它们共享 princeps，但含义不同：principle 是规则，principal 是首领或本金。

items.en: The moral sense 'a rule of right conduct' becomes common.
items.cn: 道德义“正当行为的规则”变得常见。

items.en: Modern English keeps principle for rules and truths, and principal for heads, main things, and sums of money.
items.cn: 现代英语用 principle 指规则与真理，用 principal 指校长、主要事物与本金。

note.en: The first group shares the princeps stem and the dangerous principle/principal pair; the second is about words that also mean a rule or truth.
note.cn: 第一组共享 princeps 词干与易混的 principle/principal 对，第二组看同样表示“规则”或“真理”的词。

entries.definition: chief; a school head; a sum of money. It comes from principalis, not principium.
entries.definitionCN: 主要的；校长；本金。它来自 principalis，而非 principium。

entries.definition: acting according to moral principles. It is principle plus -ed.
entries.definitionCN: 按道德原则行事的。它是 principle 加 -ed。

entries.definition: a royal ruler, from princeps 'first man'.
entries.definitionCN: 王子；亲王，来自 princeps“第一人”。

entries.definition: a statement about what must be done or what happens. It is broader and less foundational than principle.
entries.definitionCN: 关于必须做什么或会发生什么的陈述。它比 principle 更宽、更少基础性。

entries.definition: a binding rule, or a regular natural pattern. It is enforced or observed, not merely believed.
entries.definitionCN: 有约束力的规则，或自然规律。它被强制执行或被观察，而不只是被相信。

entries.definition: a set of beliefs taught by an authority. It is collective and official, unlike a personal principle.
entries.definitionCN: 权威所教的一套信念。它是集体、官方的，不同于个人原则。

normalIntro.en: Real links: Latin principium 'beginning', princeps = primus + capere, the principle/principal pair, and the phrases in principle and on principle.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：拉丁语 principium“开端”、princeps = primus + capere、principle 与 principal 这对词，以及 in principle / on principle 两个短语。

normal.en: Principium means 'beginning'. A principle is where a subject begins: the first thing you must accept.
normal.cn: principium 意为“开端”。principle 是一门学科的起点：你必须先接受的第一件事。

normal.en: Princeps is primus 'first' plus capere 'take': the chief is the one who takes first place.
normal.cn: princeps 是 primus“第一”加 capere“取”：首领就是占据第一位的人。

normal.en: Principle vs principal: a principle is a rule (from principium); a principal is a chief or a sum (from principalis).
normal.cn: principle 与 principal：principle 是规则（来自 principium）；principal 是首领或本金（来自 principalis）。

normal.en: In principle means 'in theory'; on principle means 'from conviction'. One is about ideas, the other about character.
normal.cn: in principle 意为“理论上”；on principle 意为“出于信念”。一个谈想法，一个谈品格。

normal.en: A person of principle is load-bearing: the beliefs hold up the rest of the conduct.
normal.cn: a person of principle 是承重的：这些信念撑起其余的行为。

abstract.en: A principle is a rule you keep when it costs you something; otherwise it is only a preference.
abstract.cn: 原则是付出代价时仍遵守的规则；否则它只是偏好。

abstract.en: Beginnings and rules are the same word because rules are where thought starts, not where it ends.
abstract.cn: 开端与规则是同一个词，因为规则是思想的起点，而非终点。

abstract.en: The principle/principal confusion is instructive: English once used one word for both a beginning and a chief, then split the labor.
abstract.cn: principle/principal 的混淆很有启发：英语曾用一个词兼指开端与首领，后来才分工。

examples.en: The machine works on a simple principle.
examples.cn: 这台机器依一个简单原理工作。

examples.en: She refused to sign on principle.
examples.cn: 她出于原则拒绝签署。

examples.en: In principle, the two systems should be compatible.
examples.cn: 理论上，这两个系统应当兼容。

dict_mnemonic.text: “扑润色剖”——先把原则扑在纸上，再润色剖析 → principle 原则、原理

root: 拉丁语 principium“开端”，源出 princeps“第一人”= primus“第一”+ capere“取”。同根异义词：principal（主要的；校长；本金）。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of principle, all versions of 'the first thing'. It can be the first truth of a subject, the first rule of a person, the first mechanism of a machine, or the first source of things.
sensesIntro.cn: principle 的九个义项都是“第一之物”的变体。它可以是学科的第一真理、个人的第一规则、机器的第一机制，或万物的第一源头。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a load-bearing first rule that holds up everything built on it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根承重的第一规则，撑起其上的一切。

branches.en: FOUNDATION: the basic truth explains how a subject or a natural process works.
branches.cn: 基础：基本真理解释一门学科或一个自然过程如何运作。

branches.en: CONDUCT: a moral rule becomes a personal code and a reason to act.
branches.cn: 行为：道德规则变成个人准则与行动理由。

branches.en: ORIGIN: the archaic sense names the source or constituent of things.
branches.cn: 本源：古义指事物的源头或构成要素。

branches.en: THEORY: in principle separates the idea from its execution.
branches.cn: 理论：in principle 把理念与执行分开。

branches.en: TRANSFER: an operating principle can be moved from one machine to another.
branches.cn: 迁移：工作原理可以从一台机器移到另一台。

intro.en: Principle is a noun from Latin principium. English adds -ed and the negative un-, and the princeps root also gives prince, principal, and principality.
intro.cn: principle 是来自拉丁 principium 的名词。英语加 -ed 与否定 un-，princeps 词根还生成 prince、principal、principality。

latinIntro.en: Latin principium 'beginning' and princeps 'first man' share primus 'first'. Principalis gives principal, while principium gives principle: same family, different jobs.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 principium“开端”与 princeps“第一人”共享 primus“第一”。principalis 生成 principal，principium 生成 principle：同族不同职。

items.meaning: a set of rules or beliefs
chief; a school head; a sum of money
items.meaningCN: 主要的；校长；本金（同根异义）

items.meaning: a territory ruled by a prince

definition_zh: 团结；统一；整体；协调；同一性（艺术、逻辑中）
definition_en: the state of being one, joined, or in agreement
core_image: 一张网上的许多结，都连着同一根主线
scene: 排练的时候，二十几把小提琴的弓角度一致，声音像一片。 The orchestra played with remarkable unity.
sceneCN: 这里 unity 是「协调一致」（第 1 个义项：作为整体的一）；句意为乐团演奏得异常协调。许多结都连着同一根主线，正是这个词的核心画面。

derivatives.zh: 同根名词，义为「联合；工会」
同根形容词，义为「统一的；单一的」
同根动词，义为「统一；使一致」

senses.title: The state of being one
senses.definition: the condition of being joined into a single whole
senses.definitionCN: 合成为一个整体的状态
senses.example: The unity of the two halves was never fully achieved.
senses.exampleCN: 这两半始终没能真正合为一体。
senses.why: The Latin root unus, one, plus -itas names the state of being one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 unus（一）加 -itas，命名的正是「是一体」的状态。

senses.title: Agreement among people
senses.definition: the condition of people agreeing and acting together
senses.definitionCN: 人们彼此一致、共同行动的状况
senses.example: The speech called for unity in a divided country.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇讲话呼吁分裂的国家团结起来。
senses.why: People who agree are one in purpose, so the same word serves for social harmony.
senses.whyCN: 意见一致的人在目的上是同一个，因此这个词也用于社会和睦。

senses.title: Harmony of parts in a work
senses.definition: the quality in a work that makes its parts belong together
senses.definitionCN: 让作品的各部分显得同属一体的品质
senses.example: The painting has a unity of colour that holds the eye.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画在色彩上有一种统一感，把目光留在画里。
senses.why: Judging a work means checking whether its pieces return to one shape.
senses.whyCN: 评判一件作品，就是在看它的各个部分是否回到同一个形状。

senses.title: Singleness of aim
senses.definition: used of a shared purpose that directs a group
senses.definitionCN: 形容指引一个群体的共同目的
senses.example: The campaign was run with unity of purpose.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动的推进目标一致。
senses.why: One aim is the practical shape of oneness in a working group.
senses.whyCN: 一个目标，是一体性在工作群体中的实际形态。

senses.title: Sameness in logic or mathematics
senses.definition: in technical use, the fact of being a single entity or value
senses.definitionCN: 在技术用法中，指为单一实体或单一数值
senses.example: The law of identity rests on the unity of a thing with itself.
senses.exampleCN: 同一律建立在事物与自身的一体性之上。
senses.why: The oldest philosophical question is whether one thing is really one, and unity names that.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的哲学问题就是一个事物是否真为「一」，而 unity 正是这件事的名字。

intro.en: The word comes from Latin unitas, oneness, built on unus, one.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 unitas（一体），建立在 unus（一）之上。

items.en: Unus meant one, and unitas named the state of being one.
items.cn: unus 意为「一」，unitas 则是「一体」的状态。

items.en: The word passed into French and then into English.
items.cn: 该词经法语传入英语。

items.en: English used unity for religious and social oneness.
items.cn: 英语用 unity 表示宗教与社会的一体。

items.en: Political writing made unity a standard word for agreement.
items.cn: 政治写作使 unity 成为表示一致的标准用词。

items.en: Criticism borrowed it for harmony in art and music.
items.cn: 文艺批评借它表示艺术与音乐中的协调。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the uni- family, and the near-meaning group covers harmony and agreement.
note.cn: 形近组是 uni- 词族，近义组覆盖和谐与一致的说法。

entries.definition: to join
a joining or a workers body
forming one whole
not common
entries.definitionCN: 不寻常的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: agreement of parts together
support within a group
sticking together as one
separation into parts

normalIntro.en: The word is the noun of oneness, so it covers a body, a crowd, a picture, and a purpose.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「一体」的名词，因此覆盖整体、人群、画面与目标。

normal.en: Uni- is one, and -ty names the state.
normal.cn: uni- 是「一」，-ty 命名的是那种状态。

normal.en: National unity is the phrase you meet in newspapers.
normal.cn: national unity 是报纸上常见的说法。

normal.en: Unity of purpose is a fixed phrase for shared aims.
normal.cn: unity of purpose 是表示共同目标的固定说法。

normal.en: Unity is uncountable, unlike union.
normal.cn: 与 union 不同，unity 不可数。

normal.en: Unite is the act, union the body, unity the condition.
normal.cn: unite 是动作，union 是实体，unity 是状况。

abstract.en: Picture many threads tied to a single line.
abstract.cn: 想象许多线系在同一根主线上。

abstract.en: See a choir breathe together before the first word.
abstract.cn: 看合唱团在第一个字前一起吸气。

abstract.en: Hear a hall agree without a single voice raised.
abstract.cn: 听满厅一致，没有一个人出声反对。

examples.en: The new leader promised to restore unity to the party.
examples.cn: 这位新领袖承诺让党内恢复团结。

examples.en: There is a striking unity between the two designs.
examples.cn: 两个设计之间有惊人的一致性。

examples.en: The novel is admired for the unity of its structure.
examples.cn: 这部小说的结构统一性为人称道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尤尼替」——尤尼是「一」，替是「替上」，众人替成一个，就是团结。

root: 拉丁语 unus（一）+ 名词词尾 -itas 构成 unitas（一体），经古法语进入英语

sensesIntro.en: One state, being one, appears as a whole, a crowd, a work of art, a shared aim, and a logical value.
sensesIntro.cn: 一种状态，是一体，表现为整体、人群、艺术作品、共同目标与逻辑上的单一。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: many threads knotted to the same main line.
core.cn: 核心意象：许多根线都系在同一根主线上。

branches.en: The whole branch: parts that have become one thing.
branches.cn: 整体分支：合成一物的各部分。

branches.en: The crowd branch: people in agreement.
branches.cn: 人群分支：意见一致的人们。

branches.en: The artwork branch: colour and form that hold together.
branches.cn: 作品分支：色彩与形式相守。

branches.en: The purpose branch: a single aim guiding a group.
branches.cn: 目标分支：指引群体的单一目标。

branches.en: The logical branch: the sameness of a thing with itself.
branches.cn: 逻辑分支：事物与自身同一。

intro.en: A Latin number plus a noun suffix for state gives the abstract word.
intro.cn: 拉丁语数词加表示状态的名词后缀，得到这个抽象名词。

latinIntro.en: Unus and unitas are the Latin sources for unity, unite, and union.
latinIntro.cn: unus 与 unitas 是 unity、unite、union 的拉丁来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态的拉丁语后缀

items.example: Union is the act and the body.
Harmony and unity are close twins.
items.exampleCN: harmony 与 unity 是近亲。

items.example: Solidarity is shared feeling, unity is one state.
items.exampleCN: solidarity 是共同情感，unity 是一体状态。
